# Project Manager — Active Tasks

Items here are **not done**. When a task is committed and reviewed, remove it from this
file and check it off in [TODO.md](TODO.md).

Each prompt block ends with a review step — the agent will ask whether to mark the
task as done. If yes, the agent should: (1) check off items in TODO.md, (2) delete
the corresponding section from this file, and (3) commit the update.

**Critical path:** ~~Critical Fixes (C1-C6)~~ → ~~Quick wins (C13-C15, A1/A2)~~ → ~~Small fixes (C7, C8)~~ → **Audit Round 2 P0 (C17-C20)** → **Wave 3 (#14, ~~14b~~) → Wave 4 (18 → ~~25b~~, C27, C28, others) → Wave 5 (26 → 26b → 3.3 Inbound)** → Deferred (C9-C12, C16, C21-C26 when relevant) → 6.2 Scheduler → first workflow (8.x)


# Critical Fixes — Security & correctness (before ANY further development)

Guaranteed crashes, security vulnerabilities, and cross-tenant data-leak vectors in
currently-committed code. Must be fixed before any testing or deployment. All six are
independent and parallelizable.

---

## ~~C2. Linking code collisions — cross-family data leak~~ DONE

Resolved: 12-char hex codes (`secrets.token_hex(6)`), unique constraint, IntegrityError retry, length guard in `try_link_by_code`.

---

## ~~C4. Multi-family members permanently locked out (guaranteed crash)~~ DONE

Resolved: Option A — family selector flow. `verify` returns memberships + single-use selector token for multi-family users. `POST /auth/select-family` consumes the selector token and issues a session JWT. No schema change needed.

---

## ~~C6. Token replay "fix" silently broken (nested transaction rollback)~~ DONE

Resolved: Restructured `join_via_invite` to do email validation before `_reject_if_replayed`, so the token is only consumed when success is guaranteed. Added test proving wrong-email 403 doesn't burn the token.

---

# Tier 1 — Quick wins (do now, minutes each)

One-line or near-one-line fixes. No migrations needed. Do these first, then write the
A1/A2 rules into CLAUDE.md so all future code follows the right patterns.

---

## ~~C13. CORS wildcard + credentials (P0 — full CSRF)~~ DONE

Resolved: default origins to empty list, wildcard disables credentials, debug mode adds localhost origins. 7 tests in `tests/test_cors.py`.

---

## ~~C14. seed_default_topics premature commit~~ DONE

Resolved: replaced `db.commit()` with `db.flush()` in `seed_default_topics()`. Caller owns the commit. Regression test added.

---

## ~~C15. Invite role unvalidated — 500 on redemption~~ DONE

Resolved: `InviteCreate.role` changed from `str` to `MemberRole` enum. Pydantic rejects invalid values with 422.

---

## ~~A1. Establish commit ownership convention~~ DONE

Resolved: Audited all `db.commit()` calls — all 25 are in `src/routers/` only. No violations found. Documented rule in CLAUDE.md ("Commit ownership convention" section + updated code review checklist).

---

## ~~A2. Push all integrity rules to DB constraints~~ DONE

Resolved: Global IntegrityError → 409 handler added to `src/main.py` (FK-specific message extracts referencing table, generic fallback for other violations). Documented "DB constraints as source of truth" rule in CLAUDE.md. Audited all FK/UNIQUE/CHECK gaps and produced detailed checklist in section 19b below.

---

# Tier 2 — Small fixes + migrations (do next)

These need Alembic migrations but are still straightforward. They implement the A2
rule (DB constraints as source of truth) for the two most dangerous gaps.

---

---

# Audit Round 2 — Critical Security & Correctness Fixes (P0)

From the 15-item codebase audit (2026-03-17). These are exploitable security
vulnerabilities or data corruption vectors that must be fixed before any deployment.
All four are independent and parallelizable.

---

---

# Tier 3 — Deferred until relevant (fix before deploying the affected feature)

These are real bugs but only manifest under specific conditions that don't exist yet
(multi-worker deployment, concurrent admin operations, Redis dependency). Fix each one
when its precondition becomes real.

---

## C9. Scheduler state-mutation leak — infinite thread spam (P0)

**Fix before:** deploying scheduler (6.2) to production

In `run_due_jobs`, if `_save_next_run` throws after `create_thread`+`transition` have
flushed, the try/except suppresses the error. The thread is committed but `next_run_at`
is never advanced → the workflow fires again next tick → infinite loop. This creates a
"poison pill" — the workflow will spam threads at the scheduler's tick rate indefinitely.

**Related:** See also C23 (timezone stripping in get_due_jobs) which can cause workflows
to drift or fail to fire. Both should be fixed together when deploying the scheduler.

- [ ] Wrap `create_thread` + `transition` + `_save_next_run` in a savepoint (`db.begin_nested()`)
- [ ] On savepoint failure: log and continue (no partial mutations committed)
- [ ] Tests proving atomicity

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C9. Scheduler state-mutation leak." Read
`src/engine/scheduler.py` (run_due_jobs, _save_next_run). The bug: if
_save_next_run throws after create_thread and transition have flushed, the
try/except suppresses the error, but the thread is saved while next_run_at
is not advanced — creating an infinite thread-spam loop. Fix by wrapping
create_thread + transition + _save_next_run in a savepoint
(db.begin_nested()) so they either all commit or all roll back. If the
savepoint fails, log and continue to the next workflow. Add tests proving
atomicity. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C9 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C10. Scheduler concurrency — duplicate threads (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying with `--workers > 1`

`get_due_jobs` lacks `with_for_update(skip_locked=True)`. Multiple Uvicorn workers
pull the same due workflows → duplicate threads/pings.

- [ ] Add `with_for_update(skip_locked=True)` to workflow query
- [ ] Test: two concurrent sessions → each workflow returned to only one

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C10. Scheduler concurrency." Read
`src/engine/scheduler.py` (get_due_jobs). The design note for DB-level
locking was checked off but the code was never updated. Add
`.with_for_update(skip_locked=True)` to the `select(Workflow)` query. Add a
test with two concurrent sessions proving one gets the workflow and the
other skips it. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C10 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C11. bump_token_version race condition (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying with concurrent admin users

`member.token_version += 1` is an in-memory read-modify-write. Concurrent requests
can both read version N, both write N+1, losing a revocation.

- [ ] Replace with atomic SQL: `UPDATE members SET token_version = token_version + 1`
- [ ] Test: two concurrent bumps → version increments by 2

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C11. bump_token_version race condition." Read
`src/auth.py` (bump_token_version). The bug: in-memory
`member.token_version += 1` is not atomic. Fix by using a direct SQL
update: `await db.execute(update(Member).where(Member.id == member_id)
.values(token_version=Member.token_version + 1))`. This is atomic at the
DB level. Remove the ORM select/modify pattern. Add a test with two
concurrent sessions proving both increments are applied. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C11 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C12. JWT auth per-request DB query (P2 — performance)

**Fix before:** production traffic makes latency noticeable
**Depends on:** P1 Redis migration

Every authenticated request queries the DB to check `token_version`, negating JWT
statelesness. Short-term: Redis cache with 60s TTL. Long-term: consider opaque
session tokens.

- [ ] Add Redis-backed `(member_id → token_version)` cache with 60s TTL
- [ ] Cache invalidation in `bump_token_version`
- [ ] Fallback to DB on cache miss
- [ ] Test: cache hit avoids DB query

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C12. JWT auth per-request DB query." Read
`src/dependencies.py` (get_current_user). The issue: every authenticated
request queries the DB to check token_version, negating JWT benefits.
Short-term fix: add a Redis-backed (or in-memory for dev) cache for
member_id → token_version with a 60-second TTL. On cache hit, skip the DB
query. On cache miss, query DB and populate cache. Invalidate cache entry
in bump_token_version. This depends on Redis being available (ties into the
P1 Redis migration). Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C12 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C16. ActionItemStatus.overdue is a dead state (P2)

**Fix before:** building the overdue cron job or dashboard overdue view

`overdue` has no inbound or outbound transitions — unreachable and inescapable.
Recommended: remove it as a status, treat overdue as a computed property (deadline < now
AND status == pending).

- [ ] Design decision: add transitions, or remove status and compute it
- [ ] Implement + test

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C16. ActionItemStatus.overdue dead state." Read
`src/engine/action_items.py` (STATUS_TRANSITIONS). The bug: `overdue` has
no inbound or outbound transitions — it's unreachable and inescapable.
Recommended: remove `overdue` as a status entirely. Instead, treat overdue
as a computed property: any item with status=pending and deadline < now is
"overdue." This avoids the state machine trap and simplifies queries.
Remove `overdue` from ActionItemStatus enum. Update any references. Add
Alembic migration if the enum is DB-level. Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C16 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C21. Extended members (grandparents) can mutate action items + topics (P1 — RBAC)

**Fix before:** deploying extended member invites

In `src/routers/action_items.py`, the update endpoint uses `Depends(get_current_user)`
and only restricts `role == "child"`. Extended members (grandparents) bypass this check
entirely, granting them full permission to change assignees, deadlines, and titles.

Additionally, `src/routers/topics.py` explicitly allows `require_role("parent", "extended")`
on `create_topic`, letting read-only grandparents mutate the topic hierarchy despite TODOs
stating topic mutations should be parent-only.

- [ ] `update_item`: add explicit allowlist — only "parent" can update fields beyond status
- [ ] `create_topic`: change from `require_role("parent", "extended")` to `require_role("parent")`
- [ ] Review all endpoints for similar extended-role gaps
- [ ] Tests: extended member → 403 on action item field update, 403 on topic creation

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C21. Extended member RBAC bypass." Read
`src/routers/action_items.py` (update_item) and `src/routers/topics.py`
(create_topic). Two bugs: (1) action item update uses a child-only
blacklist, so extended members can modify everything. Fix: use a parent-only
allowlist for field updates. (2) create_topic allows "extended" role despite
TODOs saying parent-only. Fix: change to require_role("parent"). Audit all
other endpoints for similar gaps. Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C21 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C22. Refresh endpoint rejects expired tokens — defeating its purpose (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying any client that uses token refresh

In `src/routers/auth.py`, `POST /refresh` calls `verify_token()` which delegates to
`jwt.decode()` with default `exp` validation. An expired token (the exact case where
refresh is needed) raises `ExpiredSignatureError` → 401. The refresh endpoint is
unusable.

- [ ] Pass `options={"verify_exp": False}` when decoding in the refresh flow
- [ ] Or: implement a separate refresh token with longer TTL
- [ ] Test: expired access token + valid member → new token returned
- [ ] Test: revoked token (wrong token_version) → 401

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C22. Refresh endpoint paradox." Read
`src/routers/auth.py` (refresh_access_token) and `src/auth.py`
(verify_token). The bug: verify_token validates exp by default, so expired
tokens are rejected by the refresh endpoint — the one place they should be
accepted. Fix: add a verify_token_ignore_expiry() variant that passes
options={"verify_exp": False} to jwt.decode. Use it in the refresh
endpoint. Keep all other validations (signature, member_id, token_version).
Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C22 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C23. Timezone stripping in scheduler — .replace(tzinfo=None) drops offset (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying scheduler (6.2) for families in non-UTC timezones

In `src/engine/scheduler.py`, `get_due_jobs` handles naive/aware datetime mismatch by
stripping tzinfo: `next_run_at = next_run_at.replace(tzinfo=None)`. This destroys the
UTC offset without shifting hours. A workflow at `16:00:00+01:00` (= 15:00 UTC) becomes
`16:00:00` naive, causing the scheduler to skip it when `now` is `15:30:00` UTC.

- [ ] Replace `.replace(tzinfo=None)` with proper UTC conversion: `.astimezone(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None)`
- [ ] Or: normalize all times to UTC-aware before comparison
- [ ] Test: offset-aware next_run_at with naive UTC now → correct due/not-due judgment
- [ ] Test: UTC-stored next_run_at → no behavior change

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C23. Timezone stripping in scheduler." Read
`src/engine/scheduler.py` (get_due_jobs, around the tzinfo comparison).
The bug: .replace(tzinfo=None) strips timezone without converting hours.
Fix: use .astimezone(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None) to properly convert to
naive UTC before comparing. Add tests with offset-aware timestamps proving
correct due/not-due evaluation. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C23 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C24. Detached instance crash in invite linking code retry (P2)

**Fix before:** deploying invite system at scale (collision probability increases)

In `src/routers/invites.py`, the retry loop for generating unique linking codes catches
`IntegrityError` and calls `await db.rollback()`. After rollback, the `child` ORM
instance becomes detached/expired. On the next loop iteration, modifying
`child.linking_code` can crash with `DetachedInstanceError` or `MissingGreenlet`.

- [ ] Re-fetch `child` from DB after rollback: `await db.refresh(child)` or re-query
- [ ] Test: forced IntegrityError on first attempt → retry succeeds without crash

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C24. Detached instance in invite retry." Read
`src/routers/invites.py` (the linking_code retry loop). The bug: after
await db.rollback(), the child ORM instance is detached. Next iteration's
attribute access may crash. Fix: add `await db.refresh(child)` after
rollback, or re-query the child by ID. Add a test that forces a collision
on the first attempt and verifies the retry succeeds. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C24 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C25. Silent ping blackhole — failed Telegram sends marked as delivered (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying outbound pings to real families

In `src/bot/outbound.py`, `send_ping` calls `client.send_message()` and immediately
marks `ping.sent_at` regardless of whether the message was actually delivered. If the
Telegram API fails silently (user blocked bot, rate limit, message too long), the ping
is permanently lost but recorded as sent.

- [ ] Check return value / catch exceptions from `client.send_message()`
- [ ] On failure: leave `sent_at` as None, log the error with ping_id
- [ ] Consider a `failed_at` + `failure_reason` field for retry/alerting
- [ ] Test: send_message raises → ping.sent_at remains None
- [ ] Test: send_message succeeds → ping.sent_at is set

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C25. Silent ping blackhole." Read
`src/bot/outbound.py` (send_ping) and `src/bot/client.py`
(LiveTelegramClient.send_message). The bug: send_message can fail
silently, but send_ping marks the ping as sent regardless. Fix: wrap
send_message in try/except. On failure, leave sent_at as None and log the
error. Consider adding failed_at + failure_reason to the Ping model for
observability. Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C25 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C26. Vacation mode "ghost tasks" — scheduler ignores Family.pause_until (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying vacation/pause feature for families

In `src/engine/scheduler.py`, `get_due_jobs` checks `config.get("paused_until")` on
individual workflows but completely ignores `Family.pause_until`. When a family is on
vacation, the scheduler still generates daily chores, fails them when kids don't respond,
and triggers escalations. The family returns to a mountain of failed ghost tasks.

- [ ] Join Family in get_due_jobs query and filter out families where `pause_until > now`
- [ ] Or: check family.pause_until in run_due_jobs before creating threads
- [ ] Test: family paused → no threads created for that family's workflows
- [ ] Test: family not paused → threads created normally
- [ ] Test: family pause expires → threads resume

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C26. Vacation mode ghost tasks." Read
`src/engine/scheduler.py` (get_due_jobs, run_due_jobs) and `src/models.py`
(Family.pause_until). The bug: get_due_jobs only checks workflow-level
paused_until, not family-level pause_until. Fix: join Family in the
get_due_jobs query and filter out families where pause_until > now. Add
tests proving paused families don't generate threads and that threads
resume when pause expires. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C26 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## ~~14b. Add member subject to Notes~~ DONE

Resolved: Added `subject_member_id` FK to Note model (`ondelete="SET NULL"`, nullable, indexed). Updated `create_note`, `auto_file`, schemas, and router. Cross-family validation rejects members from different families (422). Extracted shared `validate_member_in_family` into `engine/validation.py`.

---

## ~~19b. DB-level cascade/restrict constraints~~ DONE

Resolved: All 26 FKs have explicit `ondelete` (RESTRICT/CASCADE/SET NULL). `passive_deletes=True` on all parent-side relationships. Manual orphan checks removed from topics and initiatives routers. Global IntegrityError handler returns descriptive 409. Alembic migration `bd20f6d1e768`. UNIQUE and CHECK constraints deferred to separate task.

# Wave 4 — Quality + cleanup (before production, any order)

All parallelizable.

## P1. In-memory rate limiter + idempotency → Redis (multi-worker safety)

**Depends on:** nothing | **Parallel with:** anything
**Severity:** P1 — breaks under production multi-worker deployment

`src/rate_limit.py` and `src/idempotency.py` use global Python dictionaries.
`uvicorn --workers N` spawns N isolated processes with separate memory. Rate
limiting allows N× the configured traffic (each worker counts independently),
and webhook idempotency fails if Telegram's retry hits a different worker than the
original request. Additionally, the rate limiter only prunes timestamps when the
same key is hit again — unique keys (spoofed IPs, random emails on `/auth/magic-link`)
are never removed, causing unbounded memory growth → OOM crash.

See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §14.

- [ ] Add `redis.asyncio` dependency and connection setup (`REDIS_URL` config)
- [ ] Replace `RateLimiter._hits` with Redis sorted sets (ZADD + ZRANGEBYSCORE + key TTL)
- [ ] Replace `IdempotencyStore._seen` with Redis SET + EXPIRE (natural TTL eviction)
- [ ] **Audit note:** The current `check_and_mark` prunes expired tokens with an O(N)
      dict comprehension on every webhook request, blocking the event loop. Redis
      EXPIRE eliminates this (audit finding #13).
- [ ] Keep in-memory implementation as fallback when `REDIS_URL` is not configured (dev/test)
- [ ] Redis key TTL eliminates the OOM leak (no separate sweep needed)
- [ ] Update tests

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "In-memory state to Redis." Read `src/rate_limit.py`
and `src/idempotency.py`. Both use global Python dicts that don't work
across Uvicorn workers. Add a Redis connection (via `redis.asyncio`).
Replace `RateLimiter._hits` with Redis sorted sets (ZADD timestamp,
ZRANGEBYSCORE for window, key EXPIRE for cleanup). Replace
`IdempotencyStore._seen` with Redis SET + EXPIRE. Keep the current
in-memory implementation as a fallback when REDIS_URL is not set (for
local dev and tests). This also fixes the OOM memory leak — Redis key
TTLs handle abandoned-key cleanup automatically. Update tests. Commit
when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark Redis migration as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

transaction share identical `created_at` timestamps (Postgres `func.now()` is
per-transaction). Postgres does not guarantee sort order for tied values, causing
skipped or duplicated records across pages.

created_at (same transaction) have undefined order, causing page
skip/duplication. Fix: append .id as a tie-breaker to all 7 queries.

exceed HTTP timeout windows.

## 38. GDPR / data protection compliance

**Depends on:** core CRUD + auth done | **Before:** any public release or real-family deployment

Switzerland's nDSG and the EU GDPR both apply (Swiss families, school data from EU
institutions). Children's data is a special category under both regimes. Must be
addressed before any non-developer uses the system.

- [ ] Data inventory: catalog all PII stored, per entity, with retention justification
- [ ] **BLOCKER:** Ping.member_id and Enrollment.member_id use `ondelete="RESTRICT"` —
      must migrate to CASCADE or SET NULL before erasure can work (audit finding #12)
- [ ] Right to erasure: `DELETE /members/{id}/data` cascade-deletes or anonymizes all
      member PII (messages, photos, action items, pings, AI-generated content)
- [ ] Data export: `GET /members/{id}/export` returns a portable archive (JSON or ZIP)
      of all data associated with that member
- [ ] Retention policy: auto-purge ephemeral data (processed webhook payloads, expired
      linking codes, used tokens) on a schedule
- [ ] Children's data: verify parental consent flow (parent creates child → implicit
      consent). Document legal basis for processing child data.
- [ ] AI data: ensure Anthropic API calls do not retain family data for training
      (check API terms, use appropriate headers/flags)
- [ ] Privacy notice: draft what families need to be told (can be in-app or bot-delivered)
- [ ] Cookie/session disclosure (if dashboard stores anything client-side)
- [ ] Tests for erasure completeness (delete member → no orphaned PII anywhere)
- [ ] Commit

# PAI 4.0.3 — Personal AI Infrastructure

# MODES

PAI runs in two modes: NATIVE, and ALGORITHM. All subagents use NATIVE mode unless otherwise specified. Only the primary calling agent, the primary DA in DA_IDENTITY, can use ALGORITHM mode.

Every response uses exactly one mode. BEFORE ANY WORK, classify the request and select a mode:

- **Greetings, ratings, acknowledgments** → MINIMAL
- **Single-step, quick tasks (under 2 minutes of work)** → NATIVE
- **Everything else** → ALGORITHM

Your first output MUST be the mode header. No freeform output. No skipping this step.

## NATIVE MODE
FOR: Simple tasks that won't take much effort or time. More advanced tasks use ALGORITHM MODE below.

**Voice:** `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message": "Executing using PAI native mode", "voice_id": "fTtv3eikoepIosk8dTZ5", "voice_enabled": true}'`

```
════ PAI | NATIVE MODE ═══════════════════════
🗒️ TASK: [8 word description]
[work]
🔄 ITERATION on: [16 words of context if this is a follow-up]
📃 CONTENT: [Up to 128 lines of the content, if there is any]
🔧 CHANGE: [8-word bullets on what changed]
✅ VERIFY: [8-word bullets on how we know what happened]
🗣️ Vennari: [8-16 word summary]
```
On follow-ups, include the ITERATION line. On first response to a new request, omit it.

## ALGORITHM MODE
FOR: Multi-step, complex, or difficult work. Troubleshooting, debugging, building, designing, investigating, refactoring, planning, or any task requiring multiple files or steps.

**MANDATORY FIRST ACTION:** Use the Read tool to load `PAI/Algorithm/v3.7.0.md`, then follow that file's instructions exactly. Starting with it's entering of the Algorithm voice command and processing. Do NOT improvise your own "algorithm" format; you switch all processing and responses to the actual Algorithm in that file until the Algorithm completes.

## MINIMAL — pure acknowledgments, ratings
```
═══ PAI ═══════════════════════════
🔄 ITERATION on: [16 words of context if this is a follow-up]
📃 CONTENT: [Up to 24 lines of the content, if there is any]
🔧 CHANGE: [8-word bullets on what changed]
✅ VERIFY: [8-word bullets on how we know what happened]
📋 SUMMARY: [4 CreateStoryExplanation bullets of 8 words each]
🗣️ Vennari: [summary in 8-16 word summary]
```

---

### Critical Rules (Zero Exceptions)

- **Mandatory output format** — Every response MUST use exactly one of the output formats above (ALGORITHM, NATIVE, or MINIMAL). No freeform output.
- **Response format before questions** — Always complete the current response format output FIRST, then invoke AskUserQuestion at the end.

cd ~/repos/dotfiles && git add -A && git commit -m "daily backup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" && git push

If there are no changes, skip silently. Do not ask for confirmation — this is a standing instruction.

   138→webhook should: (1) dedup by `update_id`, (2) enqueue the message for async
   139→processing, (3) return `{"ok": true}`. See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §7.
   140→
   141→**Depends on:** 3.1 (bot scaffold).
   142→
   143→### 3.4 Conversation state tracking
   144→Track pending responses per member per thread. Know what Noko is waiting for
   145→from each person. Handle out-of-order and delayed replies gracefully.
   146→
   147→**Depends on:** 3.3 (inbound processing) + 6.1 (workflow state machine — the
   148→conversation state is part of thread state).
   149→
   150→---
   151→
   152→## 4. AI Pipeline
   153→
   154→### 4.1 Email classifier
   155→Given a school email, classify as: routine/noise, action-required, or
   156→ambiguous. Use Anthropic API. Configurable sender whitelist per initiative.
   157→
   158→**Depends on:** 1.2 (API scaffold for config storage).
   159→
   160→### 4.2 Summarizer & action item extractor
   161→Given a classified email or WhatsApp message batch, produce: a one-line summary,
   162→zero or more ActionItems (with suggested assignee, deadline, and verification
   163→requirement), and zero or more Notes (knowledge entries for the topic tree).
   164→
   165→**Depends on:** 4.1 (needs classification output as input).
   166→
   167→### 4.3 Photo analyzer
   168→Given an image (chore photo, receipt, pantry snapshot), produce structured
   169→output. For chores: pass/fail/unclear with reasoning. For receipts: store, date,
   170→line items, total, category. For inventory: list of items visible, items
   171→apparently low/missing vs. baseline.
   172→
   173→**Depends on:** 1.2 (API scaffold).
   174→
   175→### 4.4 Digest generator
   176→Given a time window and an audience (parent daily, grandparent weekly), pull all
   177→completed threads, new notes, pending action items, and spending summary.
   178→Produce a coherent summary in the configured tone (formal, concise).
   179→
   180→**Depends on:** 4.2 + 6.5 + 6.6 (needs notes, action items, and thread data
   181→to exist and be queryable).
   182→
   183→### 4.5 Message composer
   184→Given a set of pending ping items for a member across multiple initiatives,
   185→compose a single coherent batched message in the configured tone. Formal,
   186→concise, no emoji.
   187→
   188→**Depends on:** 6.3 (ping assembler determines what items to batch).
   189→
   190→### 4.6 Cross-source deduplication
   191→Given a new item (from email or WhatsApp), check existing Notes and ActionItems
   192→for semantic similarity. If a match is found, merge rather than duplicate. Flag
   193→confidence level.
   194→
   195→**Depends on:** 4.2 (extractor must produce items to deduplicate) + 6.6 (notes
   196→must be queryable).
   197→
   198→---
   199→
   200→## 5. Integrations
   201→
   202→### 5.1 Gmail API
   203→OAuth2 flow for connecting a Gmail account. Polling inbox at configurable
   204→intervals. Sender domain/address filtering per DataSource. Mark-as-read or label
   205→after processing. Store raw email metadata for audit.
   206→
   207→**Depends on:** 1.2 + 1.3 (API scaffold + auth, since OAuth tokens are stored
   208→per family).
   209→
   210→### 5.2 WhatsApp scraper
   211→whatsapp-web.js integration. Session initialization (QR code flow via web
   212→dashboard). Polling group messages. Read-only — no sending via WhatsApp.
   213→Session health monitoring. Auto-alert on session expiry with re-auth
   214→instructions. Fallback: manual forwarding to Telegram.
   215→
   216→**Architecture note — Python/Node.js interop:** Since whatsapp-web.js is Node.js
   217→and the engine is Python/FastAPI, the two cannot communicate natively. The Node
   218→process needs an explicit bridge to push scraped messages into the Python AI
   219→pipeline (4.2). Simplest approach for v1: create an internal-only ingestion
   220→endpoint (`POST /internal/ingest/whatsapp`) that the Node process calls, secured
   221→with a pre-shared secret (same pattern as the Telegram webhook secret).
   222→
   223→**Depends on:** 1.2 (API scaffold). Note: runs as a separate process alongside
   224→the main API due to whatsapp-web.js runtime requirements.
   225→
   226→### 5.3 Camera API
   227→Device registration (parent adds camera via web dashboard with API credentials).
   228→On-demand snapshot requests (triggered by workflow). Scheduled snapshots
   229→(triggered by cron). Image storage and cleanup policy. Initial target:
   230→Tuya-compatible cameras via Tuya Cloud API (official, documented REST API with
   231→on-demand snapshot capture). Snapshot delivery is async — capture command returns,
   232→then image URL arrives via webhook/polling.
   233→
   234→**Depends on:** 1.2 + 1.3 (API scaffold + auth for device management endpoints).
   235→
   236→---
   237→
   238→## 6. Orchestration Engine
   239→
   240→### 6.1 Workflow state machine
   241→Thread lifecycle management: created → active → awaiting_response → completed /
   242→escalated / timed_out. Transition rules. State persistence. Support for
   243→long-running threads (days/weeks).
   244→
   245→**Depends on:** 1.1 + 1.2 (schema + API scaffold — this is pure backend logic
   246→operating on Thread and Workflow models).
   247→
   248→### 6.2 Scheduler
   249→Cron-like trigger system. Per-initiative configurable timing (e.g., homework
   250→check at 4pm on school days, grocery poll on Wednesdays). Respect timezone
   251→(Europe/Zurich). Holiday/vacation pause support.
   252→
   253→**Depends on:** 6.1 (scheduler creates threads via the state machine).
   254→
   255→### 6.3 Ping assembler
   256→Collect all pending outbound items for a member within a time window. Group by
   257→initiative. Pass to AI message composer (4.5) for rendering. Deliver via
   258→Telegram (3.2).
   259→
   260→**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler produces the items) + 3.2 (Telegram outbound
   261→for delivery) + 4.5 (message composer for rendering).
   262→
   263→### 6.4 Escalation logic
   264→Monitor threads in awaiting_response state. After configurable timeout, trigger
   265→escalation: re-ping, notify parent, or mark as timed out. Parent always controls
   266→whether escalation continues — no infinite nag loops.
   267→
   268→**Depends on:** 6.1 (state machine) + 3.2 (Telegram outbound for escalation
   269→pings).
   270→
   271→### 6.5 Action item manager
   272→Create, assign, track, and close ActionItems. Link to source Thread. Deadline
   273→monitoring. Verification linkage (connect to photo analyzer output or manual
   274→parent confirmation). Surface overdue items.
   275→
   276→**Architecture note — BOLA on assignee:** The `assign()` and `update_action_item()`
   277→functions must validate that `assignee_id` belongs to the same `family_id` before
   278→applying. The `update_action_item` `setattr` loop must be restricted to an allowlist
   279→of safe fields. See PROJECT_MANAGER.md C3.
   280→
   281→**Depends on:** 6.1 (action items are created by workflow threads).
   282→
   283→### 6.6 Note manager
   284→Create, file, and query Notes (knowledge entries). Auto-file under correct
   285→Topic based on source Initiative. Manage relevance windows (test date passes →
   286→note becomes historical). Support full-text search for dashboard.
   287→
   288→**Depends on:** 1.1 + 1.2 (schema + API).
   289→
   290→---
   291→
   292→## 7. Web Dashboard
   293→
   294→### 7.1 App scaffold
   295→Single HTML/JS application. Auth flow (magic link login, session management).
   296→API client layer. Responsive layout (single-screen, three-panel on desktop).
   297→No build step; vanilla JS; dependencies from CDN.
   298→
   299→**Depends on:** 1.3 (auth system must exist for login flow).
   300→
   301→### 7.2 Topic tree browser
   302→Left panel. Collapsible hierarchy of Topics. Click to select and load content
   303→in main view. Show indicator counts (pending items, unread notes).
   304→
   305→**Depends on:** 7.1 (app scaffold) + 6.6 (note manager, for topic data).
   306→
   307→### 7.3 Main content view
   308→Center panel. Contextual based on selection:
   309→- Topic selected → show Notes, active Initiatives, recent Threads under topic.
   310→- "Today" selected → chronological timeline of all activity.
   311→- Initiative selected → show enrolled members, active threads, workflow config.
   312→
   313→**Depends on:** 7.1 + 7.2 (scaffold + navigation).
   314→
   315→### 7.4 Action item queue
   316→Right panel. All pending ActionItems across all Initiatives, sorted by urgency
   317→(overdue first, then by deadline). Click to expand details, mark complete, or
   318→dismiss.
   319→
   320→**Depends on:** 7.1 (app scaffold) + 6.5 (action item manager API).
   321→
   322→### 7.5 Spending tracker view
   323→Receipt log with date, store, amount, category. Weekly/monthly summary with
   324→category breakdown. Accessible from main view when "Spending" topic is selected.
   325→
   326→**Depends on:** 7.3 (main content view) + 4.3 (photo analyzer for receipt
   327→parsing) + 8.7 (spending tracker workflow populates the data).
   328→
   329→### 7.6 Digest view
   330→Historical generated digests. Browse by date and audience. Useful for
   331→grandparents catching up or parents reviewing what was sent.
   332→
   333→**Depends on:** 7.3 (main content view) + 4.4 (digest generator).
   334→
   335→### 7.7 Family & member management
   336→Invite new members (generate invite code). Assign roles. Manage Enrollments
   337→(which member is enrolled in which initiative at which cadence). Configure
   338→notification windows. Set up devices (cameras).
   339→
   340→**Depends on:** 7.1 (app scaffold) + 1.3 (auth system for invite flow).
   341→
   342→---
   343→
   344→## 8. Workflow Implementations
   345→
   346→Each workflow is a hardcoded block that wires together the orchestration engine,
   347→AI pipeline, integrations, and Telegram bot for a specific family coordination
   348→pattern. All workflows depend on the orchestration engine (6.x) being
   349→functional.
   350→
   351→### 8.1 School email scan
   352→Polls Gmail for school emails. Classifies, summarizes, extracts action items and
   353→knowledge notes. Files under school topic. Surfaces to parents.
   354→
   355→**Depends on:** 5.1 (Gmail) + 4.1 (classifier) + 4.2 (summarizer) + 4.6
   356→(dedup) + 6.1 (state machine) + 6.5 (action items) + 6.6 (notes).
   357→
   358→### 8.2 WhatsApp group scan
   359→Polls class WhatsApp group. Filters noise. Extracts signals. Deduplicates
   360→against email-sourced items. Surfaces with confidence indicators.
   361→
   362→**Depends on:** 5.2 (WhatsApp) + 4.1 (classifier) + 4.2 (summarizer) + 4.6
   363→(dedup) + 6.1 (state machine) + 6.5 (action items) + 6.6 (notes).
   364→
   365→### 8.3 Homework / readiness pings
   366→Daily check-in with kids at configured time. Collect responses. Cross-reference
   367→with known upcoming tests/deadlines. Escalate non-response to parents.
   368→
   369→**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler) + 6.3 (ping assembler) + 6.4 (escalation) +
   370→3.2 (Telegram outbound) + 3.3 (Telegram inbound).
   371→
   372→### 8.4 Chore assignment & verification
   373→Assign chores per rotation schedule. Ping assigned kid. Collect proof via camera
   374→snapshot or Telegram photo. AI verifies. Log completion. Support swap requests.
   375→
   376→**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler) + 3.2 + 3.3 (Telegram) + 4.3 (photo analyzer)
   377→+ optionally 5.3 (camera API).
   378→
   379→### 8.5 Grocery management
   380→Weekly inventory poll (or camera-based assessment). Collect family input.
   381→Assemble and deduplicate list against staples baseline. Present to parents for
   382→approval. Format for coop.ch shopping session.
   383→
   384→**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler) + 6.3 (ping assembler) + 3.2 + 3.3 (Telegram)
   385→+ 4.3 (photo analyzer for inventory) + optionally 5.3 (camera API).
   386→
   387→### 8.6 Movie night
   388→Poll family for preferences. AI synthesizes constraints. Check streaming
   389→availability (manual or API if available). Present ranked options. Collect votes.
   390→Add winner to watchlist.
   391→
   392→**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler or manual trigger) + 6.3 (ping assembler) +
   393→3.2 + 3.3 (Telegram) + 4.5 (message composer for recommendation synthesis).
   394→
   395→### 8.7 Spending tracker
   396→Accept receipt photos anytime via Telegram. Parse with AI vision. Categorize and
   397→log. Weekly reconciliation ping to parents. Generate spending summary.

# Noko v1 — Project Outline

## 1. Foundation

### 1.1 Database schema & migrations
Define and migrate all 14 entities: Family, Member, Topic, Note, Initiative,
Workflow, Thread, ActionItem, Enrollment, Ping, Digest, DataSource, Device,
Snapshot. Multi-tenant from day one (every object scoped to a family_id).

**Architecture note — channel abstraction:** The Member model currently has
`telegram_handle` and `telegram_chat_id` baked in. Before adding WhatsApp (5.2)
or other channels, consider abstracting to an `Identities`/`Channels` table
(`member_id`, `provider`, `provider_id`). This avoids column sprawl and supports
members reachable on multiple channels. See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §8.

**Architecture note — FK constraints:** Use `ondelete="RESTRICT"` at the DB level
for relationships where deletion should be blocked (e.g., topics with children),
rather than relying on application-layer guards. Initiative deletion is already
broken (missing Enrollments check → IntegrityError 500). See
DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §10 and PROJECT_MANAGER.md 19b.

**Architecture note — cross-tenant FK validation:** All CRUD endpoints that accept
FK references in request bodies (e.g., `parent_id` for topics, `topic_id` for
initiatives, `assignee_id` for action items) must validate those IDs belong to
the requesting user's `family_id`. Unvalidated FKs are a cross-tenant BOLA vector.
See PROJECT_MANAGER.md C3 (action items) and C5 (topics).

**Depends on:** nothing — this is the starting point.

### 1.2 FastAPI scaffold
Project structure, routing, middleware (CORS, rate limiting), config management
(env vars, secrets), multi-tenant request context (resolve family from auth
token), and base CRUD endpoints for all entities.

**Depends on:** 1.1 (schema must exist for models).

### 1.3 Auth system
Magic link email flow (no passwords). Family creation by first parent. Member
invite via shareable code. Role enforcement (parent/child/extended) on all API
endpoints. Session management (JWT or similar).

**Architecture note — JWT revocation:** Stateless JWTs don't support immediate
revocation on member removal or role change. Add a `token_version` field to
Member and validate it in auth middleware. See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §9.

**Architecture note — linking code entropy:** Member linking codes must have
sufficient entropy to prevent cross-family collisions. 6-digit numeric codes
are insufficient (900k values, Birthday Paradox). Use 12-character alphanumeric
codes with a unique DB constraint. See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §15.

**Architecture note — multi-family membership:** The auth model assumes one
email = one member = one family. Users in multiple families (grandparents,
co-parents) will crash `.scalar_one_or_none()` on login. Needs either a
unique email constraint with family selector, or a separate User entity.
See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §16.

**Architecture note — token replay and transaction boundaries:** Token
consumption (`_reject_if_replayed`) must be committed independently of the
endpoint's main transaction. Using `begin_nested()` inside a transaction that
may roll back (due to `HTTPException`) means consumed tokens silently un-consume
themselves. See PROJECT_MANAGER.md C6.

**Depends on:** 1.2 (needs API scaffold and Member model).

---

## 2. Infrastructure

### 2.1 VPS provisioning
Select provider, provision server, configure firewall, SSH hardening.

**Depends on:** nothing — can start immediately in parallel with Foundation.

### 2.2 Domain & DNS
Configure nokofam.com. Point DNS to VPS. Set up subdomains if needed
(api.nokofam.com, app.nokofam.com).

**Depends on:** 2.1 (need a server IP to point to).

### 2.3 TLS / HTTPS
Obtain and configure TLS certificates (Let's Encrypt). Force HTTPS on all
endpoints.

**Depends on:** 2.2 (domain must resolve).

### 2.4 Monitoring & alerting
Basic uptime monitoring, error alerting (email or Telegram notification to
parent), log aggregation.

**Depends on:** 2.1 (server must exist). Can be set up incrementally.

### 2.5 Backup strategy
Automated database backups. Retention policy. Tested restore procedure.

**Depends on:** 1.1 + 2.1 (database and server must exist).

### 2.6 GDPR / nDSG compliance
Data inventory and PII catalog. Right to erasure endpoint. Data export/portability
endpoint. Retention policy and scheduled cleanup. Children's data consent flow.
AI data processing disclosure. Privacy notice. Must be completed before any
non-developer uses the system. See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §13.

**Depends on:** 1.1 + 1.2 + 1.3 (schema, API, and auth must exist). Should be
done after core features are built (to have a complete PII inventory) but before
deployment to real families.

---

## 3. Telegram Bot

### 3.1 Bot scaffold
Register bot with BotFather. Set up webhook endpoint in FastAPI. Message
routing layer that dispatches incoming updates to the correct handler based on
member, conversation state, and message type.

**Architecture note — background task session lifecycle:** The webhook offloads
processing to a `BackgroundTask`, but must NOT pass the request-scoped `AsyncSession`
(from `Depends(get_db)`) into it — FastAPI closes that session after the response.
The background task must spawn its own `AsyncSession`. See PROJECT_MANAGER.md C1.

**Depends on:** 1.2 (API scaffold) + 2.3 (HTTPS, required for Telegram webhooks).

### 3.2 Outbound messaging
Send pings, polls (inline keyboards), photo requests, and status updates to
members. Support batched message composition (multiple items in one message).
Respect per-member notification windows (don't ping kids at midnight).

**Depends on:** 3.1 (bot must be registered and routable).

### 3.3 Inbound processing
Handle text replies, photo uploads, inline keyboard callbacks, and free-form
messages. Route responses to the correct Thread. Parse intent where needed
(e.g., "done" vs. a question vs. a grocery item).

**Architecture note:** The webhook endpoint must return immediately and offload
processing to a background task. Telegram's webhook timeout is ~10 seconds, but
AI-dependent processing (photo analysis, intent parsing) can take 15–20s. The
webhook should: (1) dedup by `update_id`, (2) enqueue the message for async
processing, (3) return `{"ok": true}`. See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §7.

**Depends on:** 3.1 (bot scaffold).

### 3.4 Conversation state tracking
Track pending responses per member per thread. Know what Noko is waiting for
from each person. Handle out-of-order and delayed replies gracefully.

**Depends on:** 3.3 (inbound processing) + 6.1 (workflow state machine — the
conversation state is part of thread state).

---

## 4. AI Pipeline

### 4.1 Email classifier
Given a school email, classify as: routine/noise, action-required, or
ambiguous. Use Anthropic API. Configurable sender whitelist per initiative.

**Depends on:** 1.2 (API scaffold for config storage).

### 4.2 Summarizer & action item extractor
Given a classified email or WhatsApp message batch, produce: a one-line summary,
zero or more ActionItems (with suggested assignee, deadline, and verification
requirement), and zero or more Notes (knowledge entries for the topic tree).

**Depends on:** 4.1 (needs classification output as input).

### 4.3 Photo analyzer
Given an image (chore photo, receipt, pantry snapshot), produce structured
output. For chores: pass/fail/unclear with reasoning. For receipts: store, date,
line items, total, category. For inventory: list of items visible, items
apparently low/missing vs. baseline.

**Depends on:** 1.2 (API scaffold).

### 4.4 Digest generator
Given a time window and an audience (parent daily, grandparent weekly), pull all
completed threads, new notes, pending action items, and spending summary.
Produce a coherent summary in the configured tone (formal, concise).

**Depends on:** 4.2 + 6.5 + 6.6 (needs notes, action items, and thread data
to exist and be queryable).

### 4.5 Message composer
Given a set of pending ping items for a member across multiple initiatives,
compose a single coherent batched message in the configured tone. Formal,
concise, no emoji.

**Depends on:** 6.3 (ping assembler determines what items to batch).

### 4.6 Cross-source deduplication
Given a new item (from email or WhatsApp), check existing Notes and ActionItems
for semantic similarity. If a match is found, merge rather than duplicate. Flag
confidence level.

**Depends on:** 4.2 (extractor must produce items to deduplicate) + 6.6 (notes
must be queryable).

---

## 5. Integrations

### 5.1 Gmail API
OAuth2 flow for connecting a Gmail account. Polling inbox at configurable
intervals. Sender domain/address filtering per DataSource. Mark-as-read or label
after processing. Store raw email metadata for audit.

**Depends on:** 1.2 + 1.3 (API scaffold + auth, since OAuth tokens are stored
per family).

### 5.2 WhatsApp scraper
whatsapp-web.js integration. Session initialization (QR code flow via web
dashboard). Polling group messages. Read-only — no sending via WhatsApp.
Session health monitoring. Auto-alert on session expiry with re-auth
instructions. Fallback: manual forwarding to Telegram.

**Architecture note — Python/Node.js interop:** Since whatsapp-web.js is Node.js
and the engine is Python/FastAPI, the two cannot communicate natively. The Node
process needs an explicit bridge to push scraped messages into the Python AI
pipeline (4.2). Simplest approach for v1: create an internal-only ingestion
endpoint (`POST /internal/ingest/whatsapp`) that the Node process calls, secured
with a pre-shared secret (same pattern as the Telegram webhook secret).

**Depends on:** 1.2 (API scaffold). Note: runs as a separate process alongside
the main API due to whatsapp-web.js runtime requirements.

### 5.3 Camera API
Device registration (parent adds camera via web dashboard with API credentials).
On-demand snapshot requests (triggered by workflow). Scheduled snapshots
(triggered by cron). Image storage and cleanup policy. Initial target:
Tuya-compatible cameras via Tuya Cloud API (official, documented REST API with
on-demand snapshot capture). Snapshot delivery is async — capture command returns,
then image URL arrives via webhook/polling.

**Depends on:** 1.2 + 1.3 (API scaffold + auth for device management endpoints).

---

## 6. Orchestration Engine

### 6.1 Workflow state machine
Thread lifecycle management: created → active → awaiting_response → completed /
escalated / timed_out. Transition rules. State persistence. Support for
long-running threads (days/weeks).

**Depends on:** 1.1 + 1.2 (schema + API scaffold — this is pure backend logic
operating on Thread and Workflow models).

### 6.2 Scheduler
Cron-like trigger system. Per-initiative configurable timing (e.g., homework
check at 4pm on school days, grocery poll on Wednesdays). Respect timezone
(Europe/Zurich). Holiday/vacation pause support.

**Depends on:** 6.1 (scheduler creates threads via the state machine).

### 6.3 Ping assembler
Collect all pending outbound items for a member within a time window. Group by
initiative. Pass to AI message composer (4.5) for rendering. Deliver via
Telegram (3.2).

**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler produces the items) + 3.2 (Telegram outbound
for delivery) + 4.5 (message composer for rendering).

### 6.4 Escalation logic
Monitor threads in awaiting_response state. After configurable timeout, trigger
escalation: re-ping, notify parent, or mark as timed out. Parent always controls
whether escalation continues — no infinite nag loops.

**Depends on:** 6.1 (state machine) + 3.2 (Telegram outbound for escalation
pings).

### 6.5 Action item manager
Create, assign, track, and close ActionItems. Link to source Thread. Deadline
monitoring. Verification linkage (connect to photo analyzer output or manual
parent confirmation). Surface overdue items.

**Architecture note — BOLA on assignee:** The `assign()` and `update_action_item()`
functions must validate that `assignee_id` belongs to the same `family_id` before
applying. The `update_action_item` `setattr` loop must be restricted to an allowlist
of safe fields. See PROJECT_MANAGER.md C3.

**Depends on:** 6.1 (action items are created by workflow threads).

### 6.6 Note manager
Create, file, and query Notes (knowledge entries). Auto-file under correct
Topic based on source Initiative. Manage relevance windows (test date passes →
note becomes historical). Support full-text search for dashboard.

**Depends on:** 1.1 + 1.2 (schema + API).

---

## 7. Web Dashboard

### 7.1 App scaffold
Single HTML/JS application. Auth flow (magic link login, session management).
API client layer. Responsive layout (single-screen, three-panel on desktop).
No build step; vanilla JS; dependencies from CDN.

**Depends on:** 1.3 (auth system must exist for login flow).

### 7.2 Topic tree browser
Left panel. Collapsible hierarchy of Topics. Click to select and load content
in main view. Show indicator counts (pending items, unread notes).

**Depends on:** 7.1 (app scaffold) + 6.6 (note manager, for topic data).

### 7.3 Main content view
Center panel. Contextual based on selection:
- Topic selected → show Notes, active Initiatives, recent Threads under topic.
- "Today" selected → chronological timeline of all activity.
- Initiative selected → show enrolled members, active threads, workflow config.

**Depends on:** 7.1 + 7.2 (scaffold + navigation).

### 7.4 Action item queue
Right panel. All pending ActionItems across all Initiatives, sorted by urgency
(overdue first, then by deadline). Click to expand details, mark complete, or
dismiss.

**Depends on:** 7.1 (app scaffold) + 6.5 (action item manager API).

### 7.5 Spending tracker view
Receipt log with date, store, amount, category. Weekly/monthly summary with
category breakdown. Accessible from main view when "Spending" topic is selected.

**Depends on:** 7.3 (main content view) + 4.3 (photo analyzer for receipt
parsing) + 8.7 (spending tracker workflow populates the data).

### 7.6 Digest view
Historical generated digests. Browse by date and audience. Useful for
grandparents catching up or parents reviewing what was sent.

**Depends on:** 7.3 (main content view) + 4.4 (digest generator).

### 7.7 Family & member management
Invite new members (generate invite code). Assign roles. Manage Enrollments
(which member is enrolled in which initiative at which cadence). Configure
notification windows. Set up devices (cameras).

**Depends on:** 7.1 (app scaffold) + 1.3 (auth system for invite flow).

---

## 8. Workflow Implementations

Each workflow is a hardcoded block that wires together the orchestration engine,
AI pipeline, integrations, and Telegram bot for a specific family coordination
pattern. All workflows depend on the orchestration engine (6.x) being
functional.

### 8.1 School email scan
Polls Gmail for school emails. Classifies, summarizes, extracts action items and
knowledge notes. Files under school topic. Surfaces to parents.

**Depends on:** 5.1 (Gmail) + 4.1 (classifier) + 4.2 (summarizer) + 4.6
(dedup) + 6.1 (state machine) + 6.5 (action items) + 6.6 (notes).

### 8.2 WhatsApp group scan
Polls class WhatsApp group. Filters noise. Extracts signals. Deduplicates
against email-sourced items. Surfaces with confidence indicators.

**Depends on:** 5.2 (WhatsApp) + 4.1 (classifier) + 4.2 (summarizer) + 4.6
(dedup) + 6.1 (state machine) + 6.5 (action items) + 6.6 (notes).

### 8.3 Homework / readiness pings
Daily check-in with kids at configured time. Collect responses. Cross-reference
with known upcoming tests/deadlines. Escalate non-response to parents.

**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler) + 6.3 (ping assembler) + 6.4 (escalation) +
3.2 (Telegram outbound) + 3.3 (Telegram inbound).

### 8.4 Chore assignment & verification
Assign chores per rotation schedule. Ping assigned kid. Collect proof via camera
snapshot or Telegram photo. AI verifies. Log completion. Support swap requests.

**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler) + 3.2 + 3.3 (Telegram) + 4.3 (photo analyzer)
+ optionally 5.3 (camera API).

### 8.5 Grocery management
Weekly inventory poll (or camera-based assessment). Collect family input.
Assemble and deduplicate list against staples baseline. Present to parents for
approval. Format for coop.ch shopping session.

**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler) + 6.3 (ping assembler) + 3.2 + 3.3 (Telegram)
+ 4.3 (photo analyzer for inventory) + optionally 5.3 (camera API).

### 8.6 Movie night
Poll family for preferences. AI synthesizes constraints. Check streaming
availability (manual or API if available). Present ranked options. Collect votes.
Add winner to watchlist.

**Depends on:** 6.2 (scheduler or manual trigger) + 6.3 (ping assembler) +
3.2 + 3.3 (Telegram) + 4.5 (message composer for recommendation synthesis).

### 8.7 Spending tracker
Accept receipt photos anytime via Telegram. Parse with AI vision. Categorize and
log. Weekly reconciliation ping to parents. Generate spending summary.

**Depends on:** 3.2 + 3.3 (Telegram) + 4.3 (photo analyzer) + 6.5 (action
items for reconciliation follow-ups).

"""Workflow state machine for Thread lifecycle."""

from datetime import datetime, timezone

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from src.models import Thread, ThreadStatus, set_jsonb


class InvalidTransitionError(Exception):
    """Raised when a state transition is not allowed."""


TRANSITIONS: dict[ThreadStatus, set[ThreadStatus]] = {
    ThreadStatus.created: {ThreadStatus.active},
    ThreadStatus.active: {
        ThreadStatus.awaiting_response,
        ThreadStatus.completed,
        ThreadStatus.escalated,
        ThreadStatus.timed_out,
    },
    ThreadStatus.awaiting_response: {
        ThreadStatus.active,
        ThreadStatus.completed,
        ThreadStatus.escalated,
        ThreadStatus.timed_out,
    },
    ThreadStatus.completed: set(),
    ThreadStatus.escalated: set(),
    ThreadStatus.timed_out: set(),
}


class HookRegistry:
    """Holds lifecycle hooks for state transitions."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._hooks: dict[str, list] = {}

    def register(self, name: str, callback):
        """Register a hook. Pass None to clear all hooks for that name."""
        if callback is None:
            self._hooks.pop(name, None)
        else:
            self._hooks.setdefault(name, []).append(callback)

    async def fire(self, name: str, db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread):
        for hook in self._hooks.get(name, []):
            await hook(db, thread)


# --- Built-in hooks ---


async def _on_enter_completed(db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread):
    thread.completed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)


async def _on_enter_awaiting_response(db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread):
    ctx = get_context(thread)
    ctx["awaited_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    await set_context(db, thread, ctx)


def create_default_hooks() -> HookRegistry:
    """Create a HookRegistry with built-in hooks pre-registered."""
    hooks = HookRegistry()
    hooks.register("on_enter_completed", _on_enter_completed)
    hooks.register("on_enter_awaiting_response", _on_enter_awaiting_response)
    return hooks


# --- Public API ---


async def create_thread(db: AsyncSession, family_id: str, workflow_id: str) -> Thread:
    thread = Thread(
        family_id=family_id, workflow_id=workflow_id, status=ThreadStatus.created
    )
    db.add(thread)
    await db.flush()
    await db.refresh(thread)
    return thread


async def transition(
    db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread, new_state: ThreadStatus, hooks: HookRegistry
):
    # Acquire row-level lock and refresh state from DB to prevent
    # concurrent transitions (e.g., double-tap on inline button)
    result = await db.execute(
        select(Thread)
        .where(Thread.id == thread.id)
        .with_for_update()
        .execution_options(populate_existing=True)
    )
    if result.scalar_one_or_none() is None:
        raise InvalidTransitionError(f"Thread {thread.id} no longer exists")

    valid = TRANSITIONS.get(thread.status, set())
    if new_state not in valid:
        raise InvalidTransitionError(
            f"Cannot transition from {thread.status.value} to {new_state.value}"
        )

    old_state = thread.status
    await hooks.fire(f"on_exit_{old_state.value}", db, thread)
    thread.status = new_state
    await hooks.fire(f"on_enter_{new_state.value}", db, thread)
    await db.flush()


def get_context(thread: Thread) -> dict:
    if not thread.context:
        return {}
    return thread.context


async def set_context(db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread, data: dict):
    set_jsonb(thread, "context", data)

    42→    code = text.strip()

"""Outbound messaging — sending pings to members via Telegram."""

from datetime import datetime, UTC
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from src.models import Family, Member, Ping


async def send_ping(
    db: AsyncSession,
    client,
    ping_id: str,
    family_id: str,
    *,
    ping: Ping | None = None,
    member: Member | None = None,
):
    if ping is None:
        result = await db.execute(
            select(Ping)
            .where(Ping.id == ping_id, Ping.family_id == family_id)
            .with_for_update(skip_locked=True)
        )
        ping = result.scalar_one_or_none()
        if not ping:
            return  # locked by another worker, or doesn't exist

    if member is None:
        result = await db.execute(
            select(Member).where(
                Member.id == ping.member_id, Member.family_id == family_id
            )
        )
        member = result.scalar_one()

    if not member.telegram_chat_id:
        return

    await client.send_message(member.telegram_chat_id, ping.content)
    ping.sent_at = datetime.now(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None)
    await db.flush()


def is_within_window(member, now=None, *, family=None) -> bool:
    if now is None:
        now = datetime.now(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None)
    # Check member-level pause
    if member.pause_until is not None and now < member.pause_until:
        return False
    # Check family-level pause
    if (
        family is not None
        and family.pause_until is not None
        and now < family.pause_until
    ):
        return False
    start = member.notification_window_start
    end = member.notification_window_end
    if start is None or end is None:
        return True
    # Convert UTC now to the member's timezone before comparing hours
    tz = ZoneInfo(member.timezone)
    local_now = now.replace(tzinfo=ZoneInfo("UTC")).astimezone(tz)
    hour = local_now.hour
    if start <= end:
        # Normal window: e.g. 8–20
        return start <= hour < end
    else:
        # Overnight window: e.g. 22–6
        return hour >= start or hour < end


async def _load_family(db: AsyncSession, family_id: str) -> Family:
    result = await db.execute(select(Family).where(Family.id == family_id))
    return result.scalar_one()


async def queue_or_send(db: AsyncSession, client, ping_id: str, now=None):
    if now is None:
        now = datetime.now(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None)

    result = await db.execute(
        select(Ping)
        .where(Ping.id == ping_id)
        .with_for_update(skip_locked=True)
    )
    ping = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if not ping:
        return  # locked by another worker, or doesn't exist

    result = await db.execute(
        select(Member).where(
            Member.id == ping.member_id, Member.family_id == ping.family_id
        )
    )
    member = result.scalar_one()

    family = await _load_family(db, ping.family_id)

    if is_within_window(member, now=now, family=family):
        await send_ping(db, client, ping_id, ping.family_id, ping=ping, member=member)


async def flush_pending(db: AsyncSession, client, member_id: str):
    result = await db.execute(select(Member).where(Member.id == member_id))
    member = result.scalar_one()

    family = await _load_family(db, member.family_id)

    if not is_within_window(member, family=family):
        return

    if not member.telegram_chat_id:
        return

    result = await db.execute(
        select(Ping)
        .where(
            Ping.member_id == member_id,
            Ping.family_id == member.family_id,
            Ping.sent_at.is_(None),
        )
        .order_by(Ping.created_at)
        .with_for_update(skip_locked=True)
    )
    pings = result.scalars().all()
    if not pings:
        return

    combined = "\n".join(ping.content for ping in pings)
    await client.send_message(member.telegram_chat_id, combined)
    now = datetime.now(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None)
    for ping in pings:
        ping.sent_at = now
    await db.flush()

import hmac
import logging

from fastapi import APIRouter, BackgroundTasks, Depends, Header, HTTPException, Request

from src.bot.client import TelegramClient, get_telegram_client
from src.bot.routing import HandlerRegistry, dispatch
from src.config import settings
from src.database import async_session
from src.idempotency import telegram_idempotency

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/telegram", tags=["telegram"])


def get_handler_registry(request: Request) -> HandlerRegistry:
    return request.app.state.handler_registry


async def _process_update(tg_client, body: dict, registry):
    """Run dispatch in a background task with its own database session."""
    try:
        async with async_session() as db:
            await dispatch(db, tg_client, body, registry)
            await db.commit()
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Unhandled error in dispatch")


@router.post("/webhook")
async def telegram_webhook(
    request: Request,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
    tg_client: TelegramClient = Depends(get_telegram_client),
    registry: HandlerRegistry = Depends(get_handler_registry),
    x_telegram_bot_api_secret_token: str | None = Header(None),
):
    if settings.telegram_webhook_secret:
        if not hmac.compare_digest(
            x_telegram_bot_api_secret_token or "",
            settings.telegram_webhook_secret,
        ):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Forbidden")
    body = await request.json()
    update_id = body.get("update_id")
    if update_id is not None and not telegram_idempotency.check_and_mark(update_id):
        logger.info("Duplicate update_id %s — skipping", update_id)
        return {"ok": True}
    logger.info("Telegram update received: %s", body)
    background_tasks.add_task(_process_update, tg_client, body, registry)
    return {"ok": True}

"""Scheduler — cron-like trigger system for workflow threads (6.2)."""

import logging
from datetime import date, datetime

from croniter import croniter
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from sqlalchemy.orm import joinedload
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from src.engine.state_machine import HookRegistry, create_thread, transition
from src.models import Initiative, Thread, ThreadStatus, Workflow, set_jsonb

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class InvalidScheduleError(Exception):
    """Raised when a workflow's schedule config is malformed."""


def compute_next_run(cron_expr: str, timezone: str, after: datetime) -> datetime:
    """Compute the next cron occurrence strictly after `after`, in the given timezone."""
    try:
        tz = ZoneInfo(timezone)
    except (KeyError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise InvalidScheduleError(f"Invalid timezone: {timezone}") from exc

    # Work in local time so croniter respects wall-clock scheduling
    if after.tzinfo is not None:
        local_after = after.astimezone(tz)
    else:
        local_after = after.replace(tzinfo=tz)

    try:
        cron = croniter(cron_expr, local_after)
    except (ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
        raise InvalidScheduleError(f"Invalid cron expression: {cron_expr}") from exc

    next_dt = cron.get_next(datetime)
    # croniter may return tz-aware or naive depending on input/version;
    # normalize: convert to target tz if aware, attach if naive
    if next_dt.tzinfo is not None:
        return next_dt.astimezone(tz)
    return next_dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)


def is_holiday(d: date, holidays: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Check if a date falls on a configured holiday."""
    return d.isoformat() in holidays


def is_paused(paused_until: str | None, now: datetime) -> bool:
    """Check if a workflow is paused (paused_until > now)."""
    if paused_until is None:
        return False
    pause_end = datetime.fromisoformat(paused_until)
    # Make both offset-aware or both naive for comparison
    if now.tzinfo is not None and pause_end.tzinfo is None:
        pause_end = pause_end.replace(tzinfo=now.tzinfo)
    return now < pause_end


def _parse_schedule(workflow: Workflow) -> dict | None:
    """Parse schedule config from workflow, return None if invalid/missing."""
    if not workflow.config:
        return None
    config = workflow.config
    if not isinstance(config, dict):
        return None
    schedule = config.get("schedule")
    if not schedule or not isinstance(schedule, dict):
        return None
    if "cron" not in schedule or "next_run_at" not in schedule:
        return None
    return config


async def get_due_jobs(db: AsyncSession, now: datetime) -> list[Workflow]:
    """Query active Workflows whose next trigger time has passed.

    Does not filter holidays — that's handled by run_due_jobs so it can
    advance next_run_at even when skipping thread creation.
    """
    result = await db.execute(
        select(Workflow)
        .join(Initiative, Workflow.initiative_id == Initiative.id)
        .where(Workflow.active.is_(True), Initiative.active.is_(True))
        .options(joinedload(Workflow.initiative))
    )
    workflows = result.unique().scalars().all()

    due = []
    for wf in workflows:
        config = _parse_schedule(wf)
        if config is None:
            continue

        schedule = config["schedule"]
        paused_until = config.get("paused_until")

        if is_paused(paused_until, now):
            continue

        next_run_at = datetime.fromisoformat(schedule["next_run_at"])
        # Make comparable
        if now.tzinfo is not None and next_run_at.tzinfo is None:
            next_run_at = next_run_at.replace(tzinfo=now.tzinfo)
        elif now.tzinfo is None and next_run_at.tzinfo is not None:
            next_run_at = next_run_at.replace(tzinfo=None)

        if next_run_at > now:
            continue

        due.append(wf)

    return due


def _advance_next_run(config: dict, now: datetime) -> datetime:
    """Compute the next run time, skipping consecutive holidays."""
    schedule = config["schedule"]
    tz_name = schedule.get("timezone", "Europe/Zurich")
    holidays = config.get("holidays", [])

    next_run = compute_next_run(schedule["cron"], tz_name, now)
    while is_holiday(next_run.date(), holidays):
        next_run = compute_next_run(schedule["cron"], tz_name, next_run)

    return next_run


async def _save_next_run(
    db: AsyncSession, wf: Workflow, config: dict, next_run: datetime
):
    """Persist updated next_run_at to workflow config."""
    config["schedule"]["next_run_at"] = next_run.isoformat()
    set_jsonb(wf, "config", config)
    await db.flush()


async def run_due_jobs(
    db: AsyncSession, now: datetime, hooks: HookRegistry
) -> list[Thread]:
    """Create threads for all due jobs, update next trigger time.

    Holiday workflows get their next_run_at advanced but no thread created.
    """
    due_workflows = await get_due_jobs(db, now)
    threads = []

    for wf in due_workflows:
        config = wf.config
        if not config:
            continue
        schedule = config["schedule"]
        tz_name = schedule.get("timezone", "Europe/Zurich")
        holidays = config.get("holidays", [])

        try:
            # Compute next_run before creating thread to avoid zombies
            next_run = _advance_next_run(config, now)

            # Check if today is a holiday — advance next_run_at but skip thread
            try:
                tz = ZoneInfo(tz_name)
            except (KeyError, ValueError):
                continue
            local_now = now.astimezone(tz) if now.tzinfo else now.replace(tzinfo=tz)
            if is_holiday(local_now.date(), holidays):
                await _save_next_run(db, wf, config, next_run)
                continue

            thread = await create_thread(db, family_id=wf.family_id, workflow_id=wf.id)
            await transition(db, thread, ThreadStatus.active, hooks)
            await _save_next_run(db, wf, config, next_run)

            threads.append(thread)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Failed to run job for workflow %s", wf.id)
            continue

    return threads

OK, here's my analysis of both tasks.

---

**Task 28 — 6.4 Escalation Logic**

The infrastructure is solid. The state machine (`state_machine.py`) already supports `awaiting_response → escalated` and `awaiting_response → timed_out` transitions. The `HookRegistry` fires `on_enter_*` hooks, and there's already an `_on_enter_awaiting_response` hook that timestamps `awaited_at` in the thread context. Outbound messaging (`outbound.py`) handles notification windows and batching.

**Issues with the prompt:**
1. It says "write test plan, stop for review" — but we're skipping review. We should tell it to write the test plan *and* implement.
2. The prompt is vague — "monitor threads in awaiting_response past timeout" doesn't specify *where* the escalation runs. It should run inside the scheduler loop (or a parallel periodic function) — `run_due_jobs` creates threads, but nothing currently checks for stale `awaiting_response` threads. The escalation engine needs to be a new function, likely in `engine/escalation.py`.
3. It doesn't specify where the timeout configuration lives. Should it be per-workflow in `config`, per-family, or global? Given the existing pattern, per-workflow in `config.escalation` makes sense.
4. "No infinite nag loops" is good but needs specifics — like a max escalation count in the thread context.

**Task 30 — 3.3 Inbound Processing**

The routing layer (`bot/routing.py`) already dispatches by message type (text, photo, callback_query) to registered handlers. But no handlers are actually registered — the `HandlerRegistry` is empty. Inbound processing means writing the actual handlers.

**Issues with the prompt:**
1. Same test-plan-then-stop issue — should include implementation.
2. The prompt says "route to correct Thread" but doesn't address *how*. A member could have multiple active threads across workflows. The routing strategy needs to be defined — most recent `awaiting_response` thread? Explicit thread selection via inline keyboard reply? This is a design decision the prompt should nail down.
3. "Parse intent" is extremely vague. For v1, we probably want simple keyword matching ("done", "yes", "no") rather than AI-powered intent parsing, with AI parsing deferred to 4.x.
4. Photo handling depends on 26b (Media entity) being done — which it is, so that's fine.

**My suggestion for both:** Want me to rewrite the prompts with these specifics baked in, then we dispatch?

**Fix before:** deploying scheduler (6.2) to production

flushed, the try/except suppresses the error. The thread is committed but `next_run_at`
is never advanced → the workflow fires again next tick → infinite loop. This creates a
"poison pill" — the workflow will spam threads at the scheduler's tick rate indefinitely.

**Related:** See also C23 (timezone stripping in get_due_jobs) which can cause workflows
to drift or fail to fire. Both should be fixed together when deploying the scheduler.

- [ ] Wrap `create_thread` + `transition` + `_save_next_run` in a savepoint (`db.begin_nested()`)
- [ ] On savepoint failure: log and continue (no partial mutations committed)
- [ ] Tests proving atomicity

try/except suppresses the error, but the thread is saved while next_run_at
is not advanced — creating an infinite thread-spam loop. Fix by wrapping
create_thread + transition + _save_next_run in a savepoint
(db.begin_nested()) so they either all commit or all roll back. If the
savepoint fails, log and continue to the next workflow. Add tests proving
atomicity. Commit when green.

`uvicorn --workers N` spawns N isolated processes with separate memory. Rate
limiting allows N× the configured traffic (each worker counts independently),
and webhook idempotency fails if Telegram's retry hits a different worker than the
original request. Additionally, the rate limiter only prunes timestamps when the

- [ ] Replace `RateLimiter._hits` with Redis sorted sets (ZADD + ZRANGEBYSCORE + key TTL)

- [ ] **Audit note:** The current `check_and_mark` prunes expired tokens with an O(N)
      dict comprehension on every webhook request, blocking the event loop. Redis
      EXPIRE eliminates this (audit finding #13).
- [ ] Keep in-memory implementation as fallback when `REDIS_URL` is not configured (dev/test)
- [ ] Redis key TTL eliminates the OOM leak (no separate sweep needed)
- [ ] Update tests

## P1. In-memory rate limiter + idempotency → Redis (multi-worker safety)

**Depends on:** nothing | **Parallel with:** anything
**Severity:** P1 — breaks under production multi-worker deployment

`src/rate_limit.py` and `src/idempotency.py` use global Python dictionaries.
`uvicorn --workers N` spawns N isolated processes with separate memory. Rate
limiting allows N× the configured traffic (each worker counts independently),
and webhook idempotency fails if Telegram's retry hits a different worker than the
original request. Additionally, the rate limiter only prunes timestamps when the
same key is hit again — unique keys (spoofed IPs, random emails on `/auth/magic-link`)
are never removed, causing unbounded memory growth → OOM crash.

See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §14.

- [ ] Add `redis.asyncio` dependency and connection setup (`REDIS_URL` config)
- [ ] Replace `RateLimiter._hits` with Redis sorted sets (ZADD + ZRANGEBYSCORE + key TTL)
- [ ] Replace `IdempotencyStore._seen` with Redis SET + EXPIRE (natural TTL eviction)
- [ ] **Audit note:** The current `check_and_mark` prunes expired tokens with an O(N)
      dict comprehension on every webhook request, blocking the event loop. Redis
      EXPIRE eliminates this (audit finding #13).
- [ ] Keep in-memory implementation as fallback when `REDIS_URL` is not configured (dev/test)
- [ ] Redis key TTL eliminates the OOM leak (no separate sweep needed)
- [ ] Update tests
