@@ -0,0 +1,285 @@
+"""Inbound message handlers for Telegram bot (3.3).
+
+Three handlers registered in the HandlerRegistry:
+- text_handler: keyword intent + note creation
+- photo_handler: media download/save + thread attachment
+- callback_handler: inline button actions (complete/snooze)
+"""
+
+import logging
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+
+from sqlalchemy import select
+from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
+
+from src.bot.client import TelegramClient
+from src.engine.notes import create_note
+from src.engine.state_machine import (
+    HookRegistry,
+    InvalidTransitionError,
+    get_context,
+    set_context,
+    transition,
+)
+from src.media import MediaStorage, build_media_url
+from src.models import (
+    Media,
+    MediaSourceType,
+    Member,
+    Ping,
+    Thread,
+    ThreadStatus,
+    Topic,
+    Workflow,
+    Initiative,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Keywords for intent detection (case-insensitive)
+COMPLETE_KEYWORDS = {"done", "yes", "finished"}
+ACKNOWLEDGE_KEYWORDS = {"no", "skip", "later"}
+
+# Callback query action constants
+ACTION_COMPLETE = "complete"
+ACTION_SNOOZE = "snooze"
+
+INBOX_TOPIC_NAME = "Inbox"
+
+
+async def _find_awaiting_thread(
+    db: AsyncSession, member: Member
+) -> Thread | None:
+    """Find the member's most recent thread in awaiting_response status.
+
+    Traces through Ping (member_id → thread_id) since Thread has no direct
+    member_id. Returns the most recently pinged awaiting thread, or None.
+    """
+    result = await db.execute(
+        select(Thread)
+        .join(Ping, Ping.thread_id == Thread.id)
+        .where(
+            Ping.member_id == member.id,
+            Thread.family_id == member.family_id,
+            Thread.status == ThreadStatus.awaiting_response,
+        )
+        .order_by(Ping.created_at.desc(), Ping.id.desc())
+        .limit(1)
+    )
+    return result.scalar_one_or_none()
+
+
+async def _get_thread_topic_id(db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread) -> str:
+    """Get the topic_id for the initiative that owns this thread's workflow."""
+    result = await db.execute(
+        select(Initiative.topic_id)
+        .join(Workflow, Workflow.initiative_id == Initiative.id)
+        .where(Workflow.id == thread.workflow_id)
+    )
+    return result.scalar_one()
+
+
+async def _get_or_create_inbox_topic(
+    db: AsyncSession, family_id: str
+) -> Topic:
+    """Get or create an 'Inbox' topic for unrouted notes."""
+    result = await db.execute(
+        select(Topic).where(
+            Topic.family_id == family_id,
+            Topic.name == INBOX_TOPIC_NAME,
+        )
+    )
+    topic = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+    if topic is not None:
+        return topic
+    topic = Topic(family_id=family_id, name=INBOX_TOPIC_NAME, sort_order=999)
+    db.add(topic)
+    await db.flush()
+    await db.refresh(topic)
+    return topic
+
+
+async def text_handler(
+    db: AsyncSession,
+    tg_client: TelegramClient,
+    member: Member,
+    message: dict,
+    *,
+    hooks: HookRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Handle incoming text messages.
+
+    Intent detection (keyword-based, no AI):
+    - "done"/"yes"/"finished" → complete the awaiting thread
+    - "no"/"skip"/"later" → acknowledge, leave thread active
+    - anything else → create a Note under the thread's topic (or Inbox if no thread)
+    """
+    text = message.get("text", "").strip()
+    chat_id = str(message.get("chat", {}).get("id", ""))
+    word = text.lower()
+
+    thread = await _find_awaiting_thread(db, member)
+
+    if thread and word in COMPLETE_KEYWORDS:
+        await transition(db, thread, ThreadStatus.completed, hooks)
+        await tg_client.send_message(chat_id, "Got it — marked as done!")
+        return
+
+    if thread and word in ACKNOWLEDGE_KEYWORDS:
+        await tg_client.send_message(
+            chat_id, "No worries, I'll check back later."
+        )
+        return
+
+    # Free-form text → create a Note
+    if thread:
+        topic_id = await _get_thread_topic_id(db, thread)
+    else:
+        inbox = await _get_or_create_inbox_topic(db, member.family_id)
+        topic_id = inbox.id
+
+    await create_note(
+        db,
+        member.family_id,
+        topic_id,
+        text,
+        source="telegram",
+        subject_member_id=member.id,
+    )
+    await tg_client.send_message(chat_id, "Noted!")
+
+
+async def photo_handler(
+    db: AsyncSession,
+    tg_client: TelegramClient,
+    member: Member,
+    message: dict,
+    *,
+    hooks: HookRegistry,
+    media_storage: MediaStorage,
+) -> None:
+    """Handle incoming photo messages.
+
+    Downloads the largest photo size, saves via MediaStorage, creates a Media
+    record, and either attaches to an awaiting thread or creates an unrouted note.
+    """
+    chat_id = str(message.get("chat", {}).get("id", ""))
+    photos = message.get("photo", [])
+    if not photos:
+        return
+
+    # Telegram sends multiple sizes; last is largest
+    largest = max(photos, key=lambda p: p.get("file_size", 0))
+    file_id = largest["file_id"]
+
+    # Download and save
+    data = await tg_client.download_file(file_id)
+    key = media_storage.save(data, "jpg")
+    internal_url = build_media_url(member.family_id, key)
+
+    media = Media(
+        family_id=member.family_id,
+        uploader_member_id=member.id,
+        content_type="image/jpeg",
+        internal_url=internal_url,
+        source_type=MediaSourceType.telegram,
+    )
+    db.add(media)
+    await db.flush()

+"""Escalation logic — monitor awaiting_response threads and take action (6.4)."""
+
+import logging
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+from sqlalchemy import select
+from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
+from sqlalchemy.orm import joinedload
+
+from src.engine.state_machine import (
+    HookRegistry,
+    get_context,
+    set_context,
+    transition,
+)
+from src.models import Member, MemberRole, Ping, Thread, ThreadStatus
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Defaults when workflow config has no escalation section
+_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MINUTES = 60
+_DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 3
+_DEFAULT_NOTIFY_PARENT = True
+
+
+def _to_naive_utc(dt: datetime) -> datetime:
+    """Normalize a datetime to naive UTC for safe comparison."""
+    if dt.tzinfo is not None:
+        return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
+    return dt
+
+
+def _get_escalation_config(thread: Thread) -> dict:
+    """Read escalation config from the thread's workflow, with defaults."""
+    workflow = thread.workflow
+    if workflow and workflow.config and isinstance(workflow.config, dict):
+        esc = workflow.config.get("escalation", {})
+        if isinstance(esc, dict):
+            return {
+                "timeout_minutes": esc.get("timeout_minutes", _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MINUTES),
+                "max_retries": esc.get("max_retries", _DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES),
+                "notify_parent": esc.get("notify_parent", _DEFAULT_NOTIFY_PARENT),
+            }
+    return {
+        "timeout_minutes": _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MINUTES,
+        "max_retries": _DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES,
+        "notify_parent": _DEFAULT_NOTIFY_PARENT,
+    }
+
+
+async def _find_first_parent(db: AsyncSession, family_id: str) -> Member | None:
+    """Find the first parent-role member in a family."""
+    result = await db.execute(
+        select(Member)
+        .where(Member.family_id == family_id, Member.role == MemberRole.parent)
+        .order_by(Member.created_at)
+        .limit(1)
+    )
+    return result.scalar_one_or_none()
+
+
+async def _bump_escalation(
+    db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread, ctx: dict, escalation_count: int, now_utc: datetime
+):
+    """Increment escalation_count and reset awaited_at in thread context."""
+    ctx["escalation_count"] = escalation_count + 1
+    ctx["awaited_at"] = now_utc.isoformat()
+    await set_context(db, thread, ctx)
+
+
+async def check_escalations(
+    db: AsyncSession, now: datetime, hooks: HookRegistry
+) -> list[dict]:
+    """Check all awaiting_response threads and escalate if timed out.
+
+    Returns a list of action dicts describing what was done, for logging/testing:
+        {"thread_id": ..., "action": "re_ping" | "notify_parent" | "timed_out"}
+    """
+    now_utc = _to_naive_utc(now)
+
+    result = await db.execute(
+        select(Thread)
+        .where(Thread.status == ThreadStatus.awaiting_response)
+        .options(joinedload(Thread.workflow))
+    )
+    threads = result.unique().scalars().all()
+
+    actions = []
+    parent_cache: dict[str, Member | None] = {}
+
+    for thread in threads:
+        ctx = get_context(thread)
+        awaited_at_str = ctx.get("awaited_at")
+        if not awaited_at_str:
+            logger.warning("Thread %s in awaiting_response but no awaited_at", thread.id)
+            continue
+
+        awaited_at = _to_naive_utc(datetime.fromisoformat(awaited_at_str))
+
+        esc_config = _get_escalation_config(thread)
+        timeout_minutes = esc_config["timeout_minutes"]
+        max_retries = esc_config["max_retries"]
+        notify_parent = esc_config["notify_parent"]
+
+        elapsed_minutes = (now_utc - awaited_at).total_seconds() / 60
+        if elapsed_minutes < timeout_minutes:
+            continue  # Not yet timed out
+
+        escalation_count = ctx.get("escalation_count", 0)
+
+        if escalation_count > max_retries:
+            # Past max retries — transition to timed_out
+            await transition(db, thread, ThreadStatus.timed_out, hooks)
+            actions.append({"thread_id": thread.id, "action": "timed_out"})
+
+        elif escalation_count == max_retries:
+            # At max retries — notify parent if configured
+            if notify_parent:
+                fid = thread.family_id
+                if fid not in parent_cache:
+                    parent_cache[fid] = await _find_first_parent(db, fid)
+                parent = parent_cache[fid]
+                if parent:
+                    ping = Ping(
+                        family_id=thread.family_id,
+                        thread_id=thread.id,
+                        member_id=parent.id,
+                        content="No response received for thread. Escalation limit reached.",
+                    )
+                    db.add(ping)
+                    actions.append({"thread_id": thread.id, "action": "notify_parent"})
+
+            # Increment count so next check transitions to timed_out
+            await _bump_escalation(db, thread, ctx, escalation_count, now_utc)
+            await db.flush()
+
+        else:
+            # Below max retries — re-ping the target member
+            target_member_id = ctx.get("target_member_id")
+            if not target_member_id:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "Thread %s has no target_member_id in context, skipping re-ping",
+                    thread.id,
+                )
+                continue
+
+            ping = Ping(
+                family_id=thread.family_id,
+                thread_id=thread.id,
+                member_id=target_member_id,
+                content="Reminder: please respond to the previous message.",
+            )
+            db.add(ping)
+
+            await _bump_escalation(db, thread, ctx, escalation_count, now_utc)
+            await db.flush()
+
+            actions.append({"thread_id": thread.id, "action": "re_ping"})
+
+    return actions

+    workflow = thread.workflow
+    if workflow and workflow.config and isinstance(workflow.config, dict):
+        esc = workflow.config.get("escalation", {})
+        if isinstance(esc, dict):
+            return {
+                "timeout_minutes": esc.get("timeout_minutes", _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MINUTES),
+                "max_retries": esc.get("max_retries", _DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES),
+                "notify_parent": esc.get("notify_parent", _DEFAULT_NOTIFY_PARENT),
+            }
+    return {
+        "timeout_minutes": _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MINUTES,
+        "max_retries": _DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES,
+        "notify_parent": _DEFAULT_NOTIFY_PARENT,
+    }
+
+
+async def _find_first_parent(db: AsyncSession, family_id: str) -> Member | None:
+    """Find the first parent-role member in a family."""
+    result = await db.execute(
+        select(Member)
+        .where(Member.family_id == family_id, Member.role == MemberRole.parent)
+        .order_by(Member.created_at)
+        .limit(1)
+    )
+    return result.scalar_one_or_none()
+
+
+async def _bump_escalation(
+    db: AsyncSession, thread: Thread, ctx: dict, escalation_count: int, now_utc: datetime
+):
+    """Increment escalation_count and reset awaited_at in thread context."""
+    ctx["escalation_count"] = escalation_count + 1
+    ctx["awaited_at"] = now_utc.isoformat()
+    await set_context(db, thread, ctx)
+
+
+async def check_escalations(
+    db: AsyncSession, now: datetime, hooks: HookRegistry
+) -> list[dict]:
+    """Check all awaiting_response threads and escalate if timed out.
+
+    Returns a list of action dicts describing what was done, for logging/testing:
+        {"thread_id": ..., "action": "re_ping" | "notify_parent" | "timed_out"}
+    """
+    now_utc = _to_naive_utc(now)
+
+    result = await db.execute(
+        select(Thread)
+        .where(Thread.status == ThreadStatus.awaiting_response)
+        .options(joinedload(Thread.workflow))
+    )
+    threads = result.unique().scalars().all()
+
+    actions = []
+    parent_cache: dict[str, Member | None] = {}
+
+    for thread in threads:
+        ctx = get_context(thread)
+        awaited_at_str = ctx.get("awaited_at")
+        if not awaited_at_str:
+            logger.warning("Thread %s in awaiting_response but no awaited_at", thread.id)
+            continue
+
+        awaited_at = _to_naive_utc(datetime.fromisoformat(awaited_at_str))
+
+        esc_config = _get_escalation_config(thread)
+        timeout_minutes = esc_config["timeout_minutes"]
+        max_retries = esc_config["max_retries"]
+        notify_parent = esc_config["notify_parent"]
+
+        elapsed_minutes = (now_utc - awaited_at).total_seconds() / 60
+        if elapsed_minutes < timeout_minutes:
+            continue  # Not yet timed out
+
+        escalation_count = ctx.get("escalation_count", 0)
+
+        if escalation_count > max_retries:
+            # Past max retries — transition to timed_out
+            await transition(db, thread, ThreadStatus.timed_out, hooks)
+            actions.append({"thread_id": thread.id, "action": "timed_out"})
+
+        elif escalation_count == max_retries:
+            # At max retries — notify parent if configured
+            if notify_parent:
+                fid = thread.family_id
+                if fid not in parent_cache:
+                    parent_cache[fid] = await _find_first_parent(db, fid)
+                parent = parent_cache[fid]
+                if parent:
+                    ping = Ping(
+                        family_id=thread.family_id,
+                        thread_id=thread.id,
+                        member_id=parent.id,
+                        content="No response received for thread. Escalation limit reached.",
+                    )
+                    db.add(ping)
+                    actions.append({"thread_id": thread.id, "action": "notify_parent"})
+
+            # Increment count so next check transitions to timed_out
+            await _bump_escalation(db, thread, ctx, escalation_count, now_utc)
+            await db.flush()
+
+        else:
+            # Below max retries — re-ping the target member
+            target_member_id = ctx.get("target_member_id")
+            if not target_member_id:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "Thread %s has no target_member_id in context, skipping re-ping",
+                    thread.id,
+                )
+                continue
+
+            ping = Ping(
+                family_id=thread.family_id,
+                thread_id=thread.id,
+                member_id=target_member_id,
+                content="Reminder: please respond to the previous message.",
+            )
+            db.add(ping)
+
+            await _bump_escalation(db, thread, ctx, escalation_count, now_utc)
+            await db.flush()
+
+            actions.append({"thread_id": thread.id, "action": "re_ping"})
+
+    return actions

# Noko v1 — Features, User Stories & Context

## Product Summary

Noko is a family coordination assistant. A Telegram bot handles day-to-day
interactions with family members (pings, polls, photo collection, quick
responses). A web dashboard gives parents an overview of everything: upcoming
items, knowledge accumulated by the system, action items, and spending. A
backend orchestration engine manages multi-day, multi-party workflows with
stateful conversation tracking, escalation logic, and AI-powered summarization.

The system is multi-tenant from day one. Each family is a fully isolated tenant.

The tone is intentionally neutral, slightly formal and robotic. Noko is a tool,
not a family member.


---


## Feature List

### F01 — Family onboarding
Create a family. First parent signs up via magic link (email, no password).
Family gets a set of sensible default topics (School, Household, Family). Parent
customizes from there.

### F02 — Member management
Parents invite members by generating an invite code in the web dashboard. Kids
are set up by a parent (parent enters name, assigns role, links Telegram
handle). Extended family members (grandparents) are invited the same way.
Roles: parent (full admin), child (receives pings, responds), extended
(receives digests, views dashboard).

### F03 — Topic hierarchy
Nestable organizational categories. Default set: School (with per-child
subtopics), Household (Chores, Groceries), Family (Entertainment, Finances).
Parents can add, rename, rearrange, or archive topics. Topics accumulate Notes
regardless of whether any Initiative is active.

### F04 — Knowledge base (Notes)
The system continuously builds a knowledge base from processed emails, WhatsApp
messages, and manual input. Each Note has: content, source (which email/message),
topic (filed automatically based on source Initiative), relevance window
(optional — a test date note expires after the test), and linked members.
Browsable in the dashboard under the topic tree.

### F05 — Initiatives & enrollment
An Initiative is an active coordination effort under a topic (e.g., "Track
Simon's homework daily"). Parents create, activate, and pause Initiatives.

# Project Manager — Active Tasks

Items here are **not done**. When a task is committed and reviewed, remove it from this
file and check it off in [TODO.md](TODO.md).

Each prompt block ends with a review step — the agent will ask whether to mark the
task as done. If yes, the agent should: (1) check off items in TODO.md, (2) delete
the corresponding section from this file, and (3) commit the update.

**Critical path:** ~~Critical Fixes (C1-C6)~~ → ~~Quick wins (C13-C15, A1/A2)~~ → ~~Small fixes (C7, C8)~~ → **Audit Round 2 P0 (C17-C20)** → **Wave 3 (#14, ~~14b~~) → Wave 4 (18 → ~~25b~~, ~~C27~~, ~~C28~~, others) → Wave 5 (~~26~~ → ~~26b~~ → ~~3.3 Inbound~~)** → Deferred (C9-C12, C16, C21-C26 when relevant) → 6.2 Scheduler → first workflow (8.x)


# Critical Fixes — Security & correctness (before ANY further development)

Guaranteed crashes, security vulnerabilities, and cross-tenant data-leak vectors in
currently-committed code. Must be fixed before any testing or deployment. All six are
independent and parallelizable.

---

## ~~C2. Linking code collisions — cross-family data leak~~ DONE

Resolved: 12-char hex codes (`secrets.token_hex(6)`), unique constraint, IntegrityError retry, length guard in `try_link_by_code`.

---

## ~~C4. Multi-family members permanently locked out (guaranteed crash)~~ DONE

Resolved: Option A — family selector flow. `verify` returns memberships + single-use selector token for multi-family users. `POST /auth/select-family` consumes the selector token and issues a session JWT. No schema change needed.

---

## ~~C6. Token replay "fix" silently broken (nested transaction rollback)~~ DONE

Resolved: Restructured `join_via_invite` to do email validation before `_reject_if_replayed`, so the token is only consumed when success is guaranteed. Added test proving wrong-email 403 doesn't burn the token.

---

# Tier 1 — Quick wins (do now, minutes each)

One-line or near-one-line fixes. No migrations needed. Do these first, then write the
A1/A2 rules into CLAUDE.md so all future code follows the right patterns.

---

## ~~C13. CORS wildcard + credentials (P0 — full CSRF)~~ DONE

Resolved: default origins to empty list, wildcard disables credentials, debug mode adds localhost origins. 7 tests in `tests/test_cors.py`.

---

## ~~C14. seed_default_topics premature commit~~ DONE

Resolved: replaced `db.commit()` with `db.flush()` in `seed_default_topics()`. Caller owns the commit. Regression test added.

---

## ~~C15. Invite role unvalidated — 500 on redemption~~ DONE

Resolved: `InviteCreate.role` changed from `str` to `MemberRole` enum. Pydantic rejects invalid values with 422.

---

## ~~A1. Establish commit ownership convention~~ DONE

Resolved: Audited all `db.commit()` calls — all 25 are in `src/routers/` only. No violations found. Documented rule in CLAUDE.md ("Commit ownership convention" section + updated code review checklist).

---

## ~~A2. Push all integrity rules to DB constraints~~ DONE

Resolved: Global IntegrityError → 409 handler added to `src/main.py` (FK-specific message extracts referencing table, generic fallback for other violations). Documented "DB constraints as source of truth" rule in CLAUDE.md. Audited all FK/UNIQUE/CHECK gaps and produced detailed checklist in section 19b below.

---

# Tier 2 — Small fixes + migrations (do next)

These need Alembic migrations but are still straightforward. They implement the A2
rule (DB constraints as source of truth) for the two most dangerous gaps.

---

---

# Audit Round 2 — Critical Security & Correctness Fixes (P0)

From the 15-item codebase audit (2026-03-17). These are exploitable security
vulnerabilities or data corruption vectors that must be fixed before any deployment.
All four are independent and parallelizable.

---

---

# Tier 3 — Deferred until relevant (fix before deploying the affected feature)

These are real bugs but only manifest under specific conditions that don't exist yet
(multi-worker deployment, concurrent admin operations, Redis dependency). Fix each one
when its precondition becomes real.

---

## C9. Scheduler state-mutation leak — infinite thread spam (P0)

**Fix before:** deploying scheduler (6.2) to production

In `run_due_jobs`, if `_save_next_run` throws after `create_thread`+`transition` have
flushed, the try/except suppresses the error. The thread is committed but `next_run_at`
is never advanced → the workflow fires again next tick → infinite loop. This creates a
"poison pill" — the workflow will spam threads at the scheduler's tick rate indefinitely.

**Related:** See also C23 (timezone stripping in get_due_jobs) which can cause workflows
to drift or fail to fire. Both should be fixed together when deploying the scheduler.

- [ ] Wrap `create_thread` + `transition` + `_save_next_run` in a savepoint (`db.begin_nested()`)
- [ ] On savepoint failure: log and continue (no partial mutations committed)
- [ ] Tests proving atomicity

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C9. Scheduler state-mutation leak." Read
`src/engine/scheduler.py` (run_due_jobs, _save_next_run). The bug: if
_save_next_run throws after create_thread and transition have flushed, the
try/except suppresses the error, but the thread is saved while next_run_at
is not advanced — creating an infinite thread-spam loop. Fix by wrapping
create_thread + transition + _save_next_run in a savepoint
(db.begin_nested()) so they either all commit or all roll back. If the
savepoint fails, log and continue to the next workflow. Add tests proving
atomicity. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C9 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C10. Scheduler concurrency — duplicate threads (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying with `--workers > 1`

`get_due_jobs` lacks `with_for_update(skip_locked=True)`. Multiple Uvicorn workers
pull the same due workflows → duplicate threads/pings.

- [ ] Add `with_for_update(skip_locked=True)` to workflow query
- [ ] Test: two concurrent sessions → each workflow returned to only one

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C10. Scheduler concurrency." Read
`src/engine/scheduler.py` (get_due_jobs). The design note for DB-level
locking was checked off but the code was never updated. Add
`.with_for_update(skip_locked=True)` to the `select(Workflow)` query. Add a
test with two concurrent sessions proving one gets the workflow and the
other skips it. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C10 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C11. bump_token_version race condition (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying with concurrent admin users

`member.token_version += 1` is an in-memory read-modify-write. Concurrent requests
can both read version N, both write N+1, losing a revocation.

- [ ] Replace with atomic SQL: `UPDATE members SET token_version = token_version + 1`
- [ ] Test: two concurrent bumps → version increments by 2

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C11. bump_token_version race condition." Read
`src/auth.py` (bump_token_version). The bug: in-memory
`member.token_version += 1` is not atomic. Fix by using a direct SQL
update: `await db.execute(update(Member).where(Member.id == member_id)
.values(token_version=Member.token_version + 1))`. This is atomic at the
DB level. Remove the ORM select/modify pattern. Add a test with two
concurrent sessions proving both increments are applied. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C11 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

---

## C12. JWT auth per-request DB query (P2 — performance)

**Fix before:** production traffic makes latency noticeable
**Depends on:** P1 Redis migration

Every authenticated request queries the DB to check `token_version`, negating JWT
statelesness. Short-term: Redis cache with 60s TTL. Long-term: consider opaque
session tokens.

- [ ] Add Redis-backed `(member_id → token_version)` cache with 60s TTL
- [ ] Cache invalidation in `bump_token_version`
- [ ] Fallback to DB on cache miss
- [ ] Test: cache hit avoids DB query

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C12. JWT auth per-request DB query." Read
`src/dependencies.py` (get_current_user). The issue: every authenticated
request queries the DB to check token_version, negating JWT benefits.
Short-term fix: add a Redis-backed (or in-memory for dev) cache for
member_id → token_version with a 60-second TTL. On cache hit, skip the DB
query. On cache miss, query DB and populate cache. Invalidate cache entry
in bump_token_version. This depends on Redis being available (ties into the
P1 Redis migration). Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C12 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C16. ActionItemStatus.overdue is a dead state (P2)

**Fix before:** building the overdue cron job or dashboard overdue view

`overdue` has no inbound or outbound transitions — unreachable and inescapable.
Recommended: remove it as a status, treat overdue as a computed property (deadline < now
AND status == pending).

- [ ] Design decision: add transitions, or remove status and compute it
- [ ] Implement + test

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C16. ActionItemStatus.overdue dead state." Read
`src/engine/action_items.py` (STATUS_TRANSITIONS). The bug: `overdue` has
no inbound or outbound transitions — it's unreachable and inescapable.
Recommended: remove `overdue` as a status entirely. Instead, treat overdue
as a computed property: any item with status=pending and deadline < now is
"overdue." This avoids the state machine trap and simplifies queries.
Remove `overdue` from ActionItemStatus enum. Update any references. Add
Alembic migration if the enum is DB-level. Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C16 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C21. Extended members (grandparents) can mutate action items + topics (P1 — RBAC)

**Fix before:** deploying extended member invites

In `src/routers/action_items.py`, the update endpoint uses `Depends(get_current_user)`
and only restricts `role == "child"`. Extended members (grandparents) bypass this check
entirely, granting them full permission to change assignees, deadlines, and titles.

Additionally, `src/routers/topics.py` explicitly allows `require_role("parent", "extended")`
on `create_topic`, letting read-only grandparents mutate the topic hierarchy despite TODOs
stating topic mutations should be parent-only.

- [ ] `update_item`: add explicit allowlist — only "parent" can update fields beyond status
- [ ] `create_topic`: change from `require_role("parent", "extended")` to `require_role("parent")`
- [ ] Review all endpoints for similar extended-role gaps
- [ ] Tests: extended member → 403 on action item field update, 403 on topic creation

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C21. Extended member RBAC bypass." Read
`src/routers/action_items.py` (update_item) and `src/routers/topics.py`
(create_topic). Two bugs: (1) action item update uses a child-only
blacklist, so extended members can modify everything. Fix: use a parent-only
allowlist for field updates. (2) create_topic allows "extended" role despite
TODOs saying parent-only. Fix: change to require_role("parent"). Audit all
other endpoints for similar gaps. Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C21 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C22. Refresh endpoint rejects expired tokens — defeating its purpose (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying any client that uses token refresh

In `src/routers/auth.py`, `POST /refresh` calls `verify_token()` which delegates to
`jwt.decode()` with default `exp` validation. An expired token (the exact case where
refresh is needed) raises `ExpiredSignatureError` → 401. The refresh endpoint is
unusable.

- [ ] Pass `options={"verify_exp": False}` when decoding in the refresh flow
- [ ] Or: implement a separate refresh token with longer TTL
- [ ] Test: expired access token + valid member → new token returned
- [ ] Test: revoked token (wrong token_version) → 401

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C22. Refresh endpoint paradox." Read
`src/routers/auth.py` (refresh_access_token) and `src/auth.py`
(verify_token). The bug: verify_token validates exp by default, so expired
tokens are rejected by the refresh endpoint — the one place they should be
accepted. Fix: add a verify_token_ignore_expiry() variant that passes
options={"verify_exp": False} to jwt.decode. Use it in the refresh
endpoint. Keep all other validations (signature, member_id, token_version).
Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C22 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C23. Timezone stripping in scheduler — .replace(tzinfo=None) drops offset (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying scheduler (6.2) for families in non-UTC timezones

In `src/engine/scheduler.py`, `get_due_jobs` handles naive/aware datetime mismatch by
stripping tzinfo: `next_run_at = next_run_at.replace(tzinfo=None)`. This destroys the
UTC offset without shifting hours. A workflow at `16:00:00+01:00` (= 15:00 UTC) becomes
`16:00:00` naive, causing the scheduler to skip it when `now` is `15:30:00` UTC.

- [ ] Replace `.replace(tzinfo=None)` with proper UTC conversion: `.astimezone(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None)`
- [ ] Or: normalize all times to UTC-aware before comparison
- [ ] Test: offset-aware next_run_at with naive UTC now → correct due/not-due judgment
- [ ] Test: UTC-stored next_run_at → no behavior change

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C23. Timezone stripping in scheduler." Read
`src/engine/scheduler.py` (get_due_jobs, around the tzinfo comparison).
The bug: .replace(tzinfo=None) strips timezone without converting hours.
Fix: use .astimezone(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None) to properly convert to
naive UTC before comparing. Add tests with offset-aware timestamps proving
correct due/not-due evaluation. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C23 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C24. Detached instance crash in invite linking code retry (P2)

**Fix before:** deploying invite system at scale (collision probability increases)

In `src/routers/invites.py`, the retry loop for generating unique linking codes catches
`IntegrityError` and calls `await db.rollback()`. After rollback, the `child` ORM
instance becomes detached/expired. On the next loop iteration, modifying
`child.linking_code` can crash with `DetachedInstanceError` or `MissingGreenlet`.

- [ ] Re-fetch `child` from DB after rollback: `await db.refresh(child)` or re-query
- [ ] Test: forced IntegrityError on first attempt → retry succeeds without crash

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C24. Detached instance in invite retry." Read
`src/routers/invites.py` (the linking_code retry loop). The bug: after
await db.rollback(), the child ORM instance is detached. Next iteration's
attribute access may crash. Fix: add `await db.refresh(child)` after
rollback, or re-query the child by ID. Add a test that forces a collision
on the first attempt and verifies the retry succeeds. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C24 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C25. Silent ping blackhole — failed Telegram sends marked as delivered (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying outbound pings to real families

In `src/bot/outbound.py`, `send_ping` calls `client.send_message()` and immediately
marks `ping.sent_at` regardless of whether the message was actually delivered. If the
Telegram API fails silently (user blocked bot, rate limit, message too long), the ping
is permanently lost but recorded as sent.

- [ ] Check return value / catch exceptions from `client.send_message()`
- [ ] On failure: leave `sent_at` as None, log the error with ping_id
- [ ] Consider a `failed_at` + `failure_reason` field for retry/alerting
- [ ] Test: send_message raises → ping.sent_at remains None
- [ ] Test: send_message succeeds → ping.sent_at is set

```prompt
Read plans/TODO.md — "C25. Silent ping blackhole." Read
`src/bot/outbound.py` (send_ping) and `src/bot/client.py`
(LiveTelegramClient.send_message). The bug: send_message can fail
silently, but send_ping marks the ping as sent regardless. Fix: wrap
send_message in try/except. On failure, leave sent_at as None and log the
error. Consider adding failed_at + failure_reason to the Ping model for
observability. Add tests. Commit when green.
Then ask the user: "Ready to mark C25 as done?"
If yes, check off in plans/TODO.md and remove from plans/PROJECT_MANAGER.md.
```

## C26. Vacation mode "ghost tasks" — scheduler ignores Family.pause_until (P1)

**Fix before:** deploying vacation/pause feature for families

In `src/engine/scheduler.py`, `get_due_jobs` checks `config.get("paused_until")` on
individual workflows but completely ignores `Family.pause_until`. When a family is on
vacation, the scheduler still generates daily chores, fails them when kids don't respond,
and triggers escalations. The family returns to a mountain of failed ghost tasks.

- [ ] Join Family in get_due_jobs query and filter out families where `pause_until > now`
- [ ] Or: check family.pause_until in run_due_jobs before creating threads
- [ ] Test: family paused → no threads created for that family's workflows
- [ ] Test: family not paused → threads created normally
- [ ] Test: family pause expires → threads resume

```prompt

(Family.pause_until). The bug: get_due_jobs only checks workflow-level
paused_until, not family-level pause_until. Fix: join Family in the
```

# Wave 3 — Data model fixes (before building on top of them)

These affect the schema and engine. Items 12-16 are parallelizable. Item 17 is a
5-minute edit.

---

## ~~14b. Add member subject to Notes~~ DONE

Resolved: Added `subject_member_id` FK to Note model (`ondelete="SET NULL"`, nullable, indexed). Updated `create_note`, `auto_file`, schemas, and router. Cross-family validation rejects members from different families (422). Extracted shared `validate_member_in_family` into `engine/validation.py`.

---

## ~~19b. DB-level cascade/restrict constraints~~ DONE

Resolved: All 26 FKs have explicit `ondelete` (RESTRICT/CASCADE/SET NULL). `passive_deletes=True` on all parent-side relationships. Manual orphan checks removed from topics and initiatives routers. Global IntegrityError handler returns descriptive 409. Alembic migration `bd20f6d1e768`. UNIQUE and CHECK constraints deferred to separate task.

# Wave 4 — Quality + cleanup (before production, any order)

All parallelizable.

---

## P1. In-memory rate limiter + idempotency → Redis (multi-worker safety)

**Depends on:** nothing | **Parallel with:** anything
**Severity:** P1 — breaks under production multi-worker deployment

`src/rate_limit.py` and `src/idempotency.py` use global Python dictionaries.
`uvicorn --workers N` spawns N isolated processes with separate memory. Rate
limiting allows N× the configured traffic (each worker counts independently),
and webhook idempotency fails if Telegram's retry hits a different worker than the
original request. Additionally, the rate limiter only prunes timestamps when the
same key is hit again — unique keys (spoofed IPs, random emails on `/auth/magic-link`)
are never removed, causing unbounded memory growth → OOM crash.

See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §14.

- [ ] Add `redis.asyncio` dependency and connection setup (`REDIS_URL` config)

## 38. GDPR / data protection compliance

**Depends on:** core CRUD + auth done | **Before:** any public release or real-family deployment

Switzerland's nDSG and the EU GDPR both apply (Swiss families, school data from EU
institutions). Children's data is a special category under both regimes. Must be
addressed before any non-developer uses the system.

- [ ] Data inventory: catalog all PII stored, per entity, with retention justification
- [ ] **BLOCKER:** Ping.member_id and Enrollment.member_id use `ondelete="RESTRICT"` —
      must migrate to CASCADE or SET NULL before erasure can work (audit finding #12)
- [ ] Right to erasure: `DELETE /members/{id}/data` cascade-deletes or anonymizes all
      member PII (messages, photos, action items, pings, AI-generated content)
- [ ] Data export: `GET /members/{id}/export` returns a portable archive (JSON or ZIP)
      of all data associated with that member
- [ ] Retention policy: auto-purge ephemeral data (processed webhook payloads, expired
      linking codes, used tokens) on a schedule
- [ ] Children's data: verify parental consent flow (parent creates child → implicit
      consent). Document legal basis for processing child data.
- [ ] AI data: ensure Anthropic API calls do not retain family data for training
      (check API terms, use appropriate headers/flags)
- [ ] Privacy notice: draft what families need to be told (can be in-app or bot-delivered)
- [ ] Cookie/session disclosure (if dashboard stores anything client-side)
- [ ] Tests for erasure completeness (delete member → no orphaned PII anywhere)

```prompt
- **C31** — `join_via_invite` rollback un-consumes token (P2)
- **C32** — State machine holds DB lock during hook execution (P1)
- **IntegrityError handler masking** — hardening note, not standalone
- **Pre-deploy scheduler bundle** — C9+C10+C23+C26+C30 grouped together

None of the new items block the AI pipeline — they're in the pre-deploy scheduler bundle or deferred tier. The AI pipeline (31-33) doesn't touch the scheduler, auth, or state machine locking. So we're clear to proceed with 31 first, then 32+33.

However — **C30 (escalation locking) and C32 (state machine lock during hooks)** are both things the inbound handlers (task 30, just committed) and escalation engine (task 28, just committed) will hit in production. +"""Email classifier — categorise school/family emails by urgency."""
     ```
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import enum
+import json
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from src.ai.client import AIClient
+
+CLASSIFICATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are an email classifier for a family coordination app. Your job is to
+classify incoming school and family-related emails into exactly one category.
+
+Categories:
+- routine: Newsletters, announcements, FYI updates — no action needed.
+- action_required: Contains a deadline, permission slip, payment, RSVP,
+  or anything a parent must act on.
+- ambiguous: Unclear whether action is needed — flag for human review.
+
+Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no extra text):
+{
+  "classification": "routine" | "action_required" | "ambiguous",
+  "confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
+  "reasoning": "One sentence explaining why."
+}
+"""
+
+
+class EmailClassification(str, enum.Enum):
+    routine = "routine"
+    action_required = "action_required"
+    ambiguous = "ambiguous"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ClassificationResult:
+    classification: EmailClassification
+    confidence: float
+    reasoning: str
+
+
+async def classify_email(
+    client: AIClient,
+    subject: str,
+    body: str,
+    sender: str,
+) -> ClassificationResult:
+    """Classify a single email using the provided AI client."""
+    user_prompt = (
+        f"From: {sender}\n"
+        f"Subject: {subject}\n\n"
+        f"{body}"
+    )
+
+    raw = await client.complete(CLASSIFICATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user_prompt)
+
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return ClassificationResult(
+            classification=EmailClassification(data["classification"]),
+            confidence=float(data["confidence"]),
+            reasoning=str(data["reasoning"]),
+        )
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError):
+        return ClassificationResult(
+            classification=EmailClassification.ambiguous,
+            confidence=0.0,
+            reasoning=f"Failed to parse AI response: {raw[:200]}",
+        )

+"""AI client abstraction — Protocol + implementations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
+
+
+@runtime_checkable
+class AIClient(Protocol):
+    """Minimal interface for LLM completion calls."""
+
+    async def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str: ...
+
+
+class AnthropicAIClient:
+    """Production client wrapping the Anthropic async SDK."""
+
+    def __init__(self, api_key: str, model: str = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514") -> None:
+        import anthropic
+
+        self._client = anthropic.AsyncAnthropic(api_key=api_key)
+        self._model = model
+
+    async def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str:
+        message = await self._client.messages.create(
+            model=self._model,
+            max_tokens=1024,
+            system=system,
+            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
+        )
+        block = message.content[0]
+        return block.text if hasattr(block, "text") else str(block)

+"""Photo analyzer — structured AI analysis of images (chores, receipts, inventory)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal
+
+from src.ai.client import AIClient
+
+CHORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are a chore verification assistant. Analyze the photo and determine whether \
+the chore has been completed satisfactorily.
+
+Respond with JSON only, no other text:
+{"status": "pass" | "fail" | "unclear", "reasoning": "one sentence explanation"}\
+"""
+
+RECEIPT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are a receipt parser. Extract structured data from the receipt photo.
+
+Respond with JSON only, no other text:
+{"store": "store name", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD or null", "items": [{"name": "item", "price": 1.99}], "total": 12.99, "currency": "CHF", "category": "groceries"}\
+"""
+
+INVENTORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are an inventory assessment assistant. Analyze the photo of a storage area \
+(pantry, fridge, shelf) and compare what you see against the provided baseline \
+list of expected items.
+
+Respond with JSON only, no other text:
+{"items_visible": ["item1"], "items_low": ["item2"], "items_missing": ["item3"]}\
+"""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ChoreResult:
+    status: Literal["pass", "fail", "unclear"]
+    reasoning: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ReceiptResult:
+    store: str
+    date: str | None
+    items: list[dict]
+    total: float | None
+    currency: str
+    category: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class InventoryResult:
+    items_visible: list[str]
+    items_low: list[str]
+    items_missing: list[str]
+
+
+async def analyze_chore(
+    client: AIClient, image_b64: str, media_type: str = "image/jpeg"
+) -> ChoreResult:
+    """Analyze a chore photo and return pass/fail/unclear with reasoning."""
+    raw = await client.complete_with_image(
+        system=CHORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
+        user="Analyze this chore photo.",
+        image_b64=image_b64,
+        media_type=media_type,
+    )
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return ChoreResult(status=data["status"], reasoning=data["reasoning"])
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError):
+        return ChoreResult(status="unclear", reasoning=f"Failed to parse AI response: {raw[:200]}")
+
+
+async def analyze_receipt(
+    client: AIClient, image_b64: str, media_type: str = "image/jpeg"
+) -> ReceiptResult:
+    """Parse a receipt photo into structured data."""
+    raw = await client.complete_with_image(
+        system=RECEIPT_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
+        user="Parse this receipt.",
+        image_b64=image_b64,
+        media_type=media_type,
+    )
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return ReceiptResult(
+            store=data["store"],
+            date=data.get("date"),
+            items=data.get("items", []),
+            total=data.get("total"),
+            currency=data.get("currency", "CHF"),
+            category=data.get("category", "other"),
+        )
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError):
+        return ReceiptResult(
+            store="unknown", date=None, items=[], total=None,
+            currency="CHF", category="other",
+        )
+
+
+async def analyze_inventory(
+    client: AIClient, image_b64: str, baseline: list[str],
+    media_type: str = "image/jpeg",
+) -> InventoryResult:
+    """Assess inventory against a baseline list of expected items."""
+    raw = await client.complete_with_image(
+        system=INVENTORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
+        user=f"Assess inventory. Baseline items: {', '.join(baseline)}",
+        image_b64=image_b64,
+        media_type=media_type,
+    )
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return InventoryResult(
+            items_visible=data.get("items_visible", []),
+            items_low=data.get("items_low", []),
+            items_missing=data.get("items_missing", []),
+        )
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError):
+        return InventoryResult(items_visible=[], items_low=[], items_missing=baseline)

+
+ACTION_ITEMS_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are an action item extractor for a family coordination app. Given text,
+extract zero or more concrete action items that a family member must do.
+
+For each action item, identify:
+- title: what needs to be done (short imperative phrase)
+- assignee_hint: who should do it, if mentioned (name or role, or null)
+- deadline_hint: when it's due, if mentioned (natural language date, or null)
+- verification: how to confirm it's done, if obvious (or null)
+
+Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no extra text):
+{
+  "action_items": [
+    {
+      "title": "...",
+      "assignee_hint": "..." or null,
+      "deadline_hint": "..." or null,
+      "verification": "..." or null
+    }
+  ]
+}
+
+If there are no action items, return: {"action_items": []}
+"""
+
+NOTES_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are a knowledge extractor for a family coordination app. Given text,
+extract factual information worth remembering (dates, locations, names,
+schedules, policies, etc.) as knowledge notes.
+
+For each note, identify:
+- content: the factual statement to remember
+- topic_hint: which family topic it relates to (e.g. "School", "Household"), or null
+
+Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no extra text):
+{
+  "notes": [
+    {
+      "content": "...",
+      "topic_hint": "..." or null
+    }
+  ]
+}
+
+If there is no notable factual information, return: {"notes": []}
+"""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ActionItemSuggestion:
+    title: str
+    assignee_hint: str | None
+    deadline_hint: str | None
+    verification: str | None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class NoteSuggestion:
+    content: str
+    topic_hint: str | None
+
+
+async def summarize(client: AIClient, text: str) -> str | None:
+    """Return a one-line summary of the input text, or None on AI failure."""
+    raw = await client.complete(SUMMARIZE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, text)
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        summary = str(data["summary"]).replace("\n", " ").strip()
+        return summary
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
+        return None
+
+
+async def extract_action_items(client: AIClient, text: str) -> list[ActionItemSuggestion]:
+    """Extract zero or more action items from text."""
+    raw = await client.complete(ACTION_ITEMS_SYSTEM_PROMPT, text)
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return [
+            ActionItemSuggestion(

+                assignee_hint=item.get("assignee_hint"),
+                deadline_hint=item.get("deadline_hint"),
+                verification=item.get("verification"),
+            )
+            for item in data["action_items"]
+        ]
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError):
+        return []
+
+
+async def extract_notes(client: AIClient, text: str) -> list[NoteSuggestion]:
+    """Extract knowledge entries from text."""
+    raw = await client.complete(NOTES_SYSTEM_PROMPT, text)
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return [
+            NoteSuggestion(
+                content=str(note["content"]),
+                topic_hint=note.get("topic_hint"),
+            )
+            for note in data["notes"]
+        ]
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError):
+        return []

+"""Summarizer, action item extractor, and note extractor (4.2)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from src.ai.client import AIClient
+
+SUMMARIZE_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are a summarizer for a family coordination app. Given text (an email,
+message batch, or conversation), produce a single-line summary.
+
+Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no extra text):
+{
+  "summary": "One concise sentence summarizing the key point."
+}
+"""
+
+ACTION_ITEMS_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are an action item extractor for a family coordination app. Given text,
+extract zero or more concrete action items that a family member must do.
+
+For each action item, identify:
+- title: what needs to be done (short imperative phrase)
+- assignee_hint: who should do it, if mentioned (name or role, or null)
+- deadline_hint: when it's due, if mentioned (natural language date, or null)
+- verification: how to confirm it's done, if obvious (or null)
+
+Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no extra text):
+{
+  "action_items": [
+    {
+      "title": "...",
+      "assignee_hint": "..." or null,
+      "deadline_hint": "..." or null,
+      "verification": "..." or null
+    }
+  ]
+}
+
+If there are no action items, return: {"action_items": []}
+"""
+
+NOTES_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
+You are a knowledge extractor for a family coordination app. Given text,
+extract factual information worth remembering (dates, locations, names,
+schedules, policies, etc.) as knowledge notes.
+
+For each note, identify:
+- content: the factual statement to remember
+- topic_hint: which family topic it relates to (e.g. "School", "Household"), or null
+
+Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no extra text):
+{
+  "notes": [
+    {
+      "content": "...",
+      "topic_hint": "..." or null
+    }
+  ]
+}
+
+If there is no notable factual information, return: {"notes": []}
+"""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ActionItemSuggestion:
+    title: str
+    assignee_hint: str | None
+    deadline_hint: str | None
+    verification: str | None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class NoteSuggestion:
+    content: str
+    topic_hint: str | None
+
+
+async def summarize(client: AIClient, text: str) -> str | None:
+    """Return a one-line summary of the input text, or None on AI failure."""
+    raw = await client.complete(SUMMARIZE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, text)
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        summary = str(data["summary"]).replace("\n", " ").strip()
+        return summary
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
+        return None
+
+
+async def extract_action_items(client: AIClient, text: str) -> list[ActionItemSuggestion]:
+    """Extract zero or more action items from text."""
+    raw = await client.complete(ACTION_ITEMS_SYSTEM_PROMPT, text)
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return [
+            ActionItemSuggestion(
+                title=str(item["title"]),
+                assignee_hint=item.get("assignee_hint"),
+                deadline_hint=item.get("deadline_hint"),
+                verification=item.get("verification"),
+            )
+            for item in data["action_items"]
+        ]
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError):
+        return []
+
+
+async def extract_notes(client: AIClient, text: str) -> list[NoteSuggestion]:
+    """Extract knowledge entries from text."""
+    raw = await client.complete(NOTES_SYSTEM_PROMPT, text)
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(raw)
+        return [
+            NoteSuggestion(
+                content=str(note["content"]),
+                topic_hint=note.get("topic_hint"),
+            )
+            for note in data["notes"]
+        ]
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError):
+        return []

## P1. In-memory rate limiter + idempotency → Redis (multi-worker safety)

**Depends on:** nothing | **Parallel with:** anything
**Severity:** P1 — breaks under production multi-worker deployment

`src/rate_limit.py` and `src/idempotency.py` use global Python dictionaries.
`uvicorn --workers N` spawns N isolated processes with separate memory. Rate
limiting allows N× the configured traffic (each worker counts independently),
and webhook idempotency fails if Telegram's retry hits a different worker than the
original request. Additionally, the rate limiter only prunes timestamps when the
same key is hit again — unique keys (spoofed IPs, random emails on `/auth/magic-link`)
are never removed, causing unbounded memory growth → OOM crash.

See DESIGN_CONSIDERATIONS.md §14.

- [ ] Add `redis.asyncio` dependency and connection setup (`REDIS_URL` config)
- [ ] Replace `RateLimiter._hits` with Redis sorted sets (ZADD + ZRANGEBYSCORE + key TTL)
- [ ] Replace `IdempotencyStore._seen` with Redis SET + EXPIRE (natural TTL eviction)
- [ ] **Audit note:** The current `check_and_mark` prunes expired tokens with an O(N)
      dict comprehension on every webhook request, blocking the event loop. Redis
      EXPIRE eliminates this (audit finding #13).
- [ ] Keep in-memory implementation as fallback when `REDIS_URL` is not configured (dev/test)
- [ ] Redis key TTL eliminates the OOM leak (no separate sweep needed)
- [ ] Update tests

+"""Camera client abstraction — Protocol, mock, and Tuya Cloud API implementation.
+
+Pattern: Strategy via Protocol. CameraClient defines the interface; MockCameraClient
+provides test doubles; TuyaCameraClient wraps the real Tuya Cloud API for on-demand
+snapshot capture from IP cameras.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import hmac
+import time
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
+
+import httpx
+from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
+
+from src.media import MediaStorage, build_media_url
+from src.models import Device, Media, MediaSourceType, Snapshot
+
+
+class CameraOfflineError(Exception):
+    """Raised when a camera device is unreachable or reports offline status."""
+
+    def __init__(self, device_id: str, detail: str = "Camera is offline"):
+        self.device_id = device_id
+        self.detail = detail
+        super().__init__(f"{detail} (device_id={device_id})")
+
+
+@runtime_checkable
+class CameraClient(Protocol):
+    """Interface for camera device interaction."""
+
+    async def capture_snapshot(self, device_id: str) -> bytes:
+        """Capture a JPEG snapshot from the device. Returns raw JPEG bytes."""
+        ...
+
+    async def get_device_status(self, device_id: str) -> dict:
+        """Get device status. Returns dict with at least a 'status' key."""
+        ...
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Tuya Cloud API implementation
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TuyaCameraClient:
+    """Wraps Tuya Cloud API for on-demand snapshot capture.
+
+    Requires `tuya_credentials` in Device.config with keys:
+    - access_id: Tuya Cloud project Access ID
+    - access_secret: Tuya Cloud project Access Secret
+    - tuya_device_id: Device ID registered in Tuya Cloud
+    """
+
+    BASE_URL = "https://openapi.tuyaus.com"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        access_id: str,
+        access_secret: str,
+        *,
+        device_id_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._access_id = access_id
+        self._access_secret = access_secret
+        self._http = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0)
+        # Maps Noko device.id → Tuya device ID. Falls back to passthrough.
+        self._device_id_map = device_id_map or {}
+
+    def _resolve_device_id(self, device_id: str) -> str:
+        """Map a Noko device ID to the Tuya-side device ID."""
+        return self._device_id_map.get(device_id, device_id)
+
+    async def aclose(self) -> None:
+        """Close the underlying HTTP client. Call when done with this client."""
+        await self._http.aclose()
+
+    def _sign(self, timestamp: str, path: str) -> str:
+        """Generate HMAC-SHA256 signature for Tuya Cloud API request."""
+        string_to_sign = f"{self._access_id}{timestamp}GET\n\n\n{path}"
+        return hmac.new(
+            self._access_secret.encode(),
+            string_to_sign.encode(),
+            hashlib.sha256,
+        ).hexdigest().upper()
+
+    def _headers(self, path: str) -> dict:
+        ts = str(int(time.time() * 1000))
+        return {
+            "client_id": self._access_id,
+            "sign": self._sign(ts, path),
+            "t": ts,
+            "sign_method": "HMAC-SHA256",
+        }
+
+    async def capture_snapshot(self, device_id: str) -> bytes:
+        """Request a snapshot from a Tuya camera and download the image."""
+        device_id = self._resolve_device_id(device_id)
+        # Step 1: Request snapshot URL from Tuya
+        path = f"/v1.0/devices/{device_id}/camera-snapshot"
+        resp = await self._http.get(
+            f"{self.BASE_URL}{path}",
+            headers=self._headers(path),
+        )
+        resp.raise_for_status()
+        data = resp.json()
+
+        if not data.get("success"):
+            raise CameraOfflineError(
+                device_id,
+                detail=data.get("msg", "Tuya API returned failure"),
+            )
+
+        image_url = data.get("result", {}).get("url")
+        if not image_url:
+            raise CameraOfflineError(device_id, detail="No snapshot URL in Tuya response")
+
+        # Step 2: Download the image bytes
+        img_resp = await self._http.get(image_url)
+        img_resp.raise_for_status()
+        return img_resp.content
+
+    async def get_device_status(self, device_id: str) -> dict:
+        """Query Tuya for device online/offline status."""
+        device_id = self._resolve_device_id(device_id)
+        path = f"/v1.0/devices/{device_id}"
+        resp = await self._http.get(
+            f"{self.BASE_URL}{path}",
+            headers=self._headers(path),
+        )
+        resp.raise_for_status()
+        data = resp.json()
+
+        if not data.get("success"):
+            return {"status": "offline", "device_id": device_id}
+
+        online = data.get("result", {}).get("online", False)
+        return {
+            "status": "online" if online else "offline",
+            "device_id": device_id,
+            "raw": data.get("result", {}),
+        }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_device_config(cls, device: Device) -> TuyaCameraClient:
+        """Create a TuyaCameraClient from a Device's config.tuya_credentials."""
+        creds = (device.config or {}).get("tuya_credentials", {})
+        access_id = creds.get("access_id", "")
+        access_secret = creds.get("access_secret", "")
+        if not access_id or not access_secret:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Device {device.id} missing tuya_credentials in config"
+            )
+        # Map Noko device.id → Tuya device ID (falls back to device.id if unset)
+        device_id_map = {}
+        tuya_device_id = creds.get("tuya_device_id")
+        if tuya_device_id:
+            device_id_map[device.id] = tuya_device_id
+        return cls(
+            access_id=access_id,
+            access_secret=access_secret,
+            device_id_map=device_id_map,
+        )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Orchestration
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+async def take_snapshot(
+    db: AsyncSession,
+    camera_client: CameraClient,
+    media_storage: MediaStorage,
+    device: Device,
+    triggered_by: str = "manual",
+) -> Snapshot:
+    """Capture snapshot → store media → create records → return Snapshot.
+
+    Flush-only: does NOT commit. The calling router/workflow owns the commit.
+    """
+    # 1. Capture image from camera (pass device.id — the client maps to
+    #    vendor-specific IDs internally if needed)
+    image_bytes = await camera_client.capture_snapshot(device.id)
+
+    # 2. Save to media storage
+    storage_key = media_storage.save(image_bytes, "jpg")
+
+    # 3. Create Media record
+    internal_url = build_media_url(device.family_id, storage_key)
+    media = Media(
+        family_id=device.family_id,
+        content_type="image/jpeg",
+        internal_url=internal_url,
+        source_type=MediaSourceType.camera,
+    )
+    db.add(media)
+    await db.flush()
+
+    # 4. Create Snapshot record
+    snapshot = Snapshot(
+        family_id=device.family_id,
+        device_id=device.id,
+        media_id=media.id,
+        triggered_by=triggered_by,
+        captured_at=datetime.now(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None),
+    )
+    db.add(snapshot)
+    await db.flush()
+
+    return snapshot

+"""Gmail integration — Protocol, mock, real client, and orchestration (5.1)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import base64
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
+
+from src.ai.classifier import EmailClassification, classify_email
+from src.ai.client import AIClient
+from src.ai.summarizer import summarize
+from src.models import DataSource
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Protocol
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@runtime_checkable
+class GmailClient(Protocol):
+    """Minimal interface for Gmail operations."""
+
+    async def list_messages(self, query: str, max_results: int) -> list[dict]: ...
+
+    async def get_message(self, msg_id: str) -> dict: ...
+
+    async def mark_as_read(self, msg_id: str) -> None: ...
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Mock implementation (for tests)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@dataclass
+class MockGmailClient:
+    """Returns canned email dicts. Tracks mark_as_read calls for assertions.
+
+    list_messages parses the ``from:`` prefix from the query string and
+    filters messages by sender, mirroring what the real Gmail API does
+    server-side. This ensures poll_inbox's query-building logic is tested.
+    """
+
+    messages: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
+    marked_read: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    async def list_messages(self, query: str, max_results: int) -> list[dict]:
+        sender_filter = ""
+        for part in query.split():
+            if part.startswith("from:"):
+                sender_filter = part[len("from:"):]
+                break
+
+        filtered = self.messages
+        if sender_filter:
+            filtered = [m for m in filtered if m.get("sender", "") == sender_filter]
+        return [{"id": m["message_id"]} for m in filtered[:max_results]]
+
+    async def get_message(self, msg_id: str) -> dict:
+        for m in self.messages:
+            if m["message_id"] == msg_id:
+                return m
+        return {}
+
+    async def mark_as_read(self, msg_id: str) -> None:
+        self.marked_read.append(msg_id)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Real Google implementation
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class GoogleGmailClient:
+    """Wraps google-auth + google-api-python-client for real Gmail API access.
+
+    OAuth2 credentials (refresh token, token URI, client ID, client secret)
+    are read from DataSource.config["credentials"]. The sync Google API calls
+    are run via asyncio.to_thread to avoid blocking the event loop.
+
+    Use the async ``create()`` classmethod instead of direct construction
+    to avoid blocking the event loop during credential refresh and service
+    discovery.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, service: object, credentials: object) -> None:
+        self._service = service
+        self._credentials = credentials
+
+    @classmethod
+    async def create(cls, data_source: DataSource) -> "GoogleGmailClient":
+        """Async factory — refreshes credentials and builds service off-thread."""
+
+        def _build() -> tuple:
+            from google.auth.transport.requests import Request
+            from google.oauth2.credentials import Credentials
+            from googleapiclient.discovery import build
+
+            creds_data = data_source.config.get("credentials", {})
+            credentials = Credentials(
+                token=creds_data.get("token"),
+                refresh_token=creds_data.get("refresh_token"),
+                token_uri=creds_data.get("token_uri", "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"),
+                client_id=creds_data.get("client_id"),
+                client_secret=creds_data.get("client_secret"),
+            )
+            if credentials.expired and credentials.refresh_token:
+                credentials.refresh(Request())
+            service = build("gmail", "v1", credentials=credentials)
+            return service, credentials
+
+        service, credentials = await asyncio.to_thread(_build)
+        return cls(service=service, credentials=credentials)
+
+    async def list_messages(self, query: str, max_results: int) -> list[dict]:
+        def _list() -> list[dict]:
+            result = (
+                self._service.users()
+                .messages()
+                .list(userId="me", q=query, maxResults=max_results)
+                .execute()
+            )
+            return result.get("messages", [])
+
+        return await asyncio.to_thread(_list)
+
+    async def get_message(self, msg_id: str) -> dict:
+        def _get() -> dict:
+            msg = (
+                self._service.users()
+                .messages()
+                .get(userId="me", id=msg_id, format="full")
+                .execute()
+            )
+            headers = {h["name"]: h["value"] for h in msg.get("payload", {}).get("headers", [])}
+            body = _extract_body(msg.get("payload", {}))
+            return {
+                "message_id": msg["id"],
+                "subject": headers.get("Subject", ""),
+                "sender": headers.get("From", ""),
+                "date": headers.get("Date", ""),
+                "body": body,
+            }
+
+        return await asyncio.to_thread(_get)
+
+    async def mark_as_read(self, msg_id: str) -> None:
+        def _mark() -> None:
+            self._service.users().messages().modify(
+                userId="me",
+                id=msg_id,
+                body={"removeLabelIds": ["UNREAD"]},
+            ).execute()
+
+        await asyncio.to_thread(_mark)
+
+
+def _extract_body(payload: dict) -> str:
+    """Extract plain-text body from a Gmail message payload."""
+    if payload.get("mimeType") == "text/plain" and payload.get("body", {}).get("data"):
+        return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload["body"]["data"]).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+    for part in payload.get("parts", []):
+        result = _extract_body(part)
+        if result:
+            return result
+    return ""
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Orchestration functions
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+async def poll_inbox(client: GmailClient, data_source: DataSource) -> list[dict]:
+    """Poll inbox using sender filter from data_source config.
+
+    Returns list of {"subject", "body", "sender", "date", "message_id"}.
+    """
+    sender_filter = data_source.config.get("sender_filter", "")
+    query = f"from:{sender_filter} is:unread" if sender_filter else "is:unread"
+
+    raw_messages = await client.list_messages(query=query, max_results=50)
+
+    results = []
+    for raw in raw_messages:
+        msg_id = raw.get("id") or raw.get("message_id", "")
+        if not msg_id:
+            continue
+        detail = await client.get_message(msg_id)
+        if not detail:
+            continue
+        # For MockGmailClient, detail already has the right shape.
+        # For GoogleGmailClient, get_message returns the normalized dict.
+        results.append({
+            "subject": detail.get("subject", ""),
+            "body": detail.get("body", ""),
+            "sender": detail.get("sender", ""),
+            "date": detail.get("date", ""),
+            "message_id": detail.get("message_id", msg_id),
+        })
+
+    return results
+
+
+async def process_emails(
+    ai_client: AIClient,
+    gmail_client: GmailClient,
+    data_source: DataSource,
+) -> list[dict]:
+    """Orchestrate: poll -> classify each -> summarize action_required -> mark as read.
+
+    Two-phase approach: process all emails first, then mark as read.
+    If the process crashes mid-batch, nothing is marked read so emails
+    get retried on the next poll (idempotent, no data loss).
+    Returns processing results for logging.
+    """
+    emails = await poll_inbox(gmail_client, data_source)
+    results: list[dict] = []
+    processed_ids: list[str] = []
+
+    for email in emails:
+        try:
+            classification = await classify_email(
+                client=ai_client,
+                subject=email["subject"],
+                body=email["body"],
+                sender=email["sender"],
+            )
+
+            entry: dict = {
+                "message_id": email["message_id"],
+                "subject": email["subject"],
+                "sender": email["sender"],
+                "classification": classification.classification.value,
+                "confidence": classification.confidence,
+            }
+
+            if classification.classification == EmailClassification.action_required:
+                text = f"Subject: {email['subject']}\n\n{email['body']}"
+                summary = await summarize(ai_client, text)
+                entry["summary"] = summary
+
+            results.append(entry)
+            processed_ids.append(email["message_id"])
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Failed to process email %s", email.get("message_id"))
+            continue
+
+    # Phase 2: mark processed emails as read after all processing succeeds
+    for msg_id in processed_ids:
+        try:
+            await gmail_client.mark_as_read(msg_id)
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Failed to mark email %s as read", msg_id)
+
+    return results

+

+        summarize(ai_client, batch_text),
+        extract_notes(ai_client, batch_text),
+    )
+
+    # Persist summary as a note
+    if summary:
+        note = await create_note(
+            db,
+            family_id=request.family_id,
+            topic_id=None,
+            content=summary,
+            source=source,
+        )
+        created_notes.append(note)
+
+    # Persist extracted knowledge notes
+    for suggestion in note_suggestions:
+        note = await create_note(

+            topic_id=None,
+            content=suggestion.content,
+            source=source,
+        )
+        created_notes.append(note)
+
+    return WhatsAppIngestResponse(
+        processed=len(request.messages),

+"""WhatsApp ingestion endpoint — internal API for the Node.js scraper."""
+
+import hmac
+import logging
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Header, HTTPException, Request
+from sqlalchemy import select
+from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
+
+from src.ai.client import AIClient
+from src.config import settings
+from src.database import get_db
+from src.integrations.whatsapp import (
+    WhatsAppIngestRequest,
+    WhatsAppIngestResponse,
+    process_whatsapp_batch,
+)
+from src.models import Family
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+router = APIRouter(prefix="/internal/ingest", tags=["whatsapp"])
+
+
+def get_ai_client(request: Request):
+    """Retrieve the singleton AI client from app.state."""
+    client = request.app.state.ai_client
+    if client is None:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="AI client not configured")
+    return client
+
+
+@router.post("/whatsapp", response_model=WhatsAppIngestResponse)
+async def ingest_whatsapp(
+    body: WhatsAppIngestRequest,
+    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
+    ai_client: AIClient = Depends(get_ai_client),
+    x_internal_secret: str | None = Header(None),
+):
+    """Ingest a batch of WhatsApp messages from the Node.js scraper.
+
+    Secured with X-Internal-Secret header. Runs messages through the AI
+    pipeline (note extraction) and persists results.
+    """
+    if not settings.internal_api_secret or not hmac.compare_digest(
+        x_internal_secret or "",
+        settings.internal_api_secret,
+    ):
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Forbidden")
+
+    # Validate family exists before AI processing
+    family = await db.execute(
+        select(Family.id).where(Family.id == body.family_id)
+    )
+    if family.scalar_one_or_none() is None:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Unknown family_id")
+
+    result = await process_whatsapp_batch(db, ai_client, body)
+    await db.commit()
+
+    logger.info(
+        "WhatsApp ingest: group=%s processed=%d notes=%d",
+        body.group_name,
+        result.processed,
+        result.notes_created,
+    )
+    return result
